557.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Raag Vadhans, Ghar 1, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). If the addict does not get his drug, if the fish has no water, (nothing pleases them); (but) to those imbued with their own Husband (Lord), everyone is dear. I am a sacrifice, cut in pieces as a sacrifice, to your Name, O Master. The Master is a tree laden with fruit, whose Name is Amrit (the nectar of immortal life); those who have drunk (it) are fulfilled; I am a sacrifice to them. (O Lord,) you do not come into my sight, though you dwell with all. How is the thirsty one's thirst to go, when a wall stands between (him and) the pool? Nanak is your trader; you are the Master, (and you are) my capital. Anxiety leaves the mind only when I sing (your) praise and pray (to you). ॥4॥
557.2: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The virtuous (soul-bride) has enjoyed her Husband's love; why does the one without virtue cry out? If she becomes virtuous, then she too can go to enjoy her Husband's love. My Husband is the source of delight, dear friend; why should the bride enjoy others? If (good) deeds become the love-charm, if the mind becomes the thread, (then) the ruby, not to be had for any price, is won by threading it into the consciousness. I ask the way but do not walk it, and (yet) I say I have arrived. With you, my Husband, I am not even on speaking terms; how can I come to dwell in (your) house? O Nanak, apart from the One there is no other. If (a bride) stays attached to you, my Husband, then she enjoys her Husband's love. ॥4॥
557.3: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The peacocks have struck up their sweet calls, O sister; Saavan (the month of the rains) has come. (O Lord,) these (sights) of yours are a dagger and a noose for the bride; this (beauty of yours) has drawn me, who long (for you), with longing. I am cut in pieces as a sacrifice to the sight of you; I am a sacrifice to your Name. Because you are (mine), I have taken pride; without you, what pride have I? Break your bangles against the bed, O young bride, together with (its) side-frames and (your) arms; O young bride, adorning yourself in so many ways, (your) Husband is in love with others. Neither the bangle-seller, nor the bangles, nor those glass bangles (are of any use); may the arms that have not embraced the Husband's neck burn. All (my) friends have gone to enjoy the Husband's love; to whose door shall I, the burnt one, go? O friend, I (count myself) most well-mannered, (yet) I do not please you, my Husband, by even one (virtue). I have my plaits braided with care, and the parting of my hair is filled with vermilion; (yet) going before (him), I am not accepted; I die, grieving and grieving. As I weep, the whole world has wept; the birds of the forest have wept too; only one has not wept: the separation within my body, which has parted me from my Beloved. He came in a dream and went again; I wept, (my eyes) brimming with tears. I cannot come to you, Beloved, nor can I send anyone. Come, blessed sleep; perhaps I may see that Husband (again). The one who tells (me) a word of you, my Master, says Nanak, what should (I) give him? One should cut off one's head and give it (him) for a seat, and serve (him) without a head. Why should one not die, why not give up one's life, when the Husband has become a stranger? ॥1॥
Saavan: the month of the rains (July–August), in Punjabi poetry the season of longing for an absent husband. The chooda: the red bangles a bride puts on at her wedding.
558.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. When the mind is soiled, all is soiled; washing the body does not make the mind clean. This world is led astray by doubt; rare is the one who understands (this). O my mind, repeat the one Name; this is the treasure the True Guru has given me. If one learns the postures of the Siddhas (yogis held to be perfected), and practises (them), holding the senses in check, (still) the filth of the mind does not come off, the filth of Haumai (ego) does not go. For this mind there is no other discipline but the refuge of the True Guru. Meeting the True Guru, (the mind's attention) is turned back (from the world); nothing can be said (of it). Says Nanak: whoever, meeting the True Guru, dies (to the self) and through the Guru's Shabad lives again, the filth of the sense of mine comes off (him), and this mind becomes clean. ॥4॥
558.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through (God's) glance of grace the True Guru is served; through his glance of grace service is done; through his glance of grace this mind comes under control; through his glance of grace the mind becomes pure. O my mind, remember that True One. If you remember the One, you will find peace, and then there will be no sorrow at all. Through his glance of grace one dies (to the self) and lives; through his glance of grace the Shabad comes to dwell in the mind. Through his glance of grace the Hukam (God's will) is understood, and (one) stays merged in the Hukam. The tongue that has not tasted the Lord's essence, may that tongue burn; it stayed attached to the tastes of other pleasures, and in the love of another it found pain. The glance of the One is on all; he himself makes the difference (between them). O Nanak, meeting the True Guru, (one) has found the fruit; (God) grants the Naam and honour. ॥4॥
559.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Attachment to Maya (the world's illusion and lure) is pitch darkness; without the Guru there is no (spiritual) wisdom. Those attached to the Shabad have understood; in the love of another the world's people are ruined. O my mind, keep to the way of life of the Guru's teaching. If you dwell on the Lord God for ever and ever, you will find the door of liberation. The One is the treasure of virtues; only when he himself gives does anyone receive (it). Without the Name all are parted (from him); through the Guru's Shabad he unites (them). Crying mine, mine, they wasted away; nothing came into their hands. Meeting the True Guru, (they) met the True One and merged in the True Name. This body is (caught in) hope and desire; (God) lights the Light within (it). O Nanak, the manmukh (the self-willed) is in bondage; through the Guru (God) brings liberation. ॥4॥
559.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The faces of the happy soul-brides are ever radiant; through the Guru (they abide) in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and in love. Shedding the self from within, they ever enjoy their Husband's love. Meditate, O my mind, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har; for the True Guru has made the Lord known to me. The forsaken soul-brides wail bitterly; they do not find (the Husband's) mansion. Made ugly by the love of another, they suffer pain when they go on (to the world) beyond. The virtuous (soul-bride), enshrining the Naam in her heart, dwells on (his) virtues every day; the wife full of faults is struck by pain and wails. The one Master is the Husband of all; nothing can be said (of him). O Nanak, he himself has made (them) distinct, (and some) he has attached to the Name. ॥4॥
559.3: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Amrit Name has become ever sweet (to me), for through the Guru's Shabad its savour has come; through the true Bani (my attention) is merged in Sahaj, and (I) have enshrined the dear Lord in my mind. The Lord, in his mercy, has brought (me) to the True Guru; through the perfect True Guru (I) have meditated on the Lord's Name. Brahma revealed the word of the Vedas, (but what spread from it was) attachment to Maya. Mahadev (Shiva), the wise one, stays absorbed in his own house, (yet in him is) the darkness of tamas and much pride. Kisan (Vishnu) is ever caught up in taking incarnations; holding to whom, (then), shall the world cross over? Through the Guru, those steeped in (spiritual) wisdom in this age find the darkness of attachment ended. Through service of the True Guru comes release; through the Guru the world crosses over. The detached, imbued with the True Name, find the door of liberation. The One True Lord pervades all, and cherishes all. I, Nanak, know none but the One; the merciful One is the support of all. ॥5॥

Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu are the three gods of the Puranas; the commentators read Kisan (Krishna) here as Vishnu, of whom Krishna is held to be an incarnation. Tamas: of the three qualities of Maya, the one of darkness and inertia.
559.4: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through the Guru (come) truth, self-discipline and the essence of wisdom; through the Guru the attention is fixed on the True One. O my mind, through the Guru, keep the Naam in your heart; it stands by (you) always and goes along with you. Through the Guru, that True One is (one's) caste and honour; through the Guru, God becomes the companion within. He alone becomes Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) whom (God) himself makes so; through the Guru he himself gives glory. Through the Guru, make the true Shabad your task and keep to it; through the Guru, O Nanak, (one becomes) a support to (one's) family too. ॥4॥
560.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The tongue has taken to the Lord's taste, in Sahaj and in love; meditating on the Lord's Name, the mind is satisfied. There is lasting peace in reflecting on the True Shabad. I am ever a sacrifice to my True Guru. The eyes are content, fixing (their) attention on the One; shedding the love of another, the mind is at rest. Through the Shabad, through the Lord's Name, there is peace in the body; the fragrance of the Naam pervades the heart. O Nanak, the one on whose forehead is great good fortune (gains), through the Guru's Bani, detachment in Sahaj. ॥4॥
560.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Naam is obtained from the perfect Guru; through the True Shabad (one) merges in the True One. O mind, obtain the treasure of the Naam; accept the will of your Guru. When the filth within is removed through the Guru's Shabad, the pure Naam comes to dwell in the mind. Led astray by doubt, the world wanders about; it dies and is born, and Jam (the messenger of Death) brings it to ruin. O Nanak, fortunate are those who have meditated on the Name of the Lord and, by the Guru's grace, have enshrined (it) in the mind. ॥4॥
560.3: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Haumai is opposed to the Name; the two do not dwell in one place. In Haumai (his) service cannot be done, and so the mind goes to waste. O my mind, remember the Lord; live by the Guru's Shabad. If you obey the Hukam, then the Lord is met, and then Haumai goes from within. Haumai fills the whole body; through Haumai (one) comes to birth. Haumai is a great darkness; in Haumai no one can understand. In Haumai devotion cannot be done, and the Hukam is not understood. In Haumai the soul is in bondage; the Naam does not come to dwell in the mind. O Nanak, on meeting the True Guru, Haumai went, and then the True One came to dwell in the mind. (Then one) lives the truth, abides in the truth, and, serving the True One, merges (in him). ॥4॥
560.4: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The bed (of the heart) is one, and the one God is the Master (upon it); through the Guru (the soul-bride) enjoys the Lord, the ocean of peace. In my mind is the hope of meeting God in love. The perfect Guru unites (me with) my Beloved; I will be a sacrifice to my Guru again and again. My body is full of faults; how can I meet my perfect Beloved? She who is virtuous has found my Beloved; those virtues are not in me: how shall I meet (him), O my mother? I am worn out with trying ever so many means; O my Lord, protect poor Nanak. ॥4॥
561.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). My Lord God is beautiful, (yet) I have not known (his) worth; leaving the Lord God, I have been lured by another. How am I, so ignorant, to meet the Husband? She who pleases the Husband is the happy soul-bride; she alone, the wise one, meets the Husband. Faults are in me: how shall I find the Husband? Many are your loved ones, O Husband; I do not come to your mind. She who has enjoyed the Husband's love is the good, happy soul-bride; those virtues are not in me: what am I, the forsaken one, to do? The happy soul-bride enjoys the Husband's love day after day, for ever; will he ever clasp me, the luckless one, to his bosom? You, my Husband, are full of virtues; I am full of faults; forgive me, the virtueless one, poor Nanak. ॥5॥
561.2: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. In my mind is a great hope, O Lord: how may I obtain the sight of the Lord? Let me go and ask my True Guru, and, having asked the Guru, teach my foolish mind. The strayed mind comes to understand through the Guru's Shabad, and meditates on the Lord, Har Har, for ever. O Nanak, the one on whom my Beloved casts his glance of grace fixes his mind on the Lord's feet. I put on every kind of dress for the Husband's sake, that I may be pleasing to the True Lord God; (but) that dear Husband does not turn his eyes to me: how am I to find comfort? He for whose sake I adorn myself, that Husband of mine is in love with others. O Nanak, blessed, blessed, blessed is the happy soul-bride who has enjoyed the love of the Husband, the True, the Beautiful. Let me go and ask the happy soul-bride, beloved of the Husband: how did you find the Husband, my God? (She answers:) The True Husband cast his glance of grace upon me, (and) I gave up mine and yours. Make mind, body and soul, all of it, the Lord God's; by this path, O sister, he is met. O Nanak, (the one) on whom one's own dear God looks with his glance of grace, (that one's) light blends with the Light. Whoever brings me a message of the Lord God, to him I would give my mind and body; each day I would fan (him), do (his) service, and carry water to him. Day after day I would serve that servant of the Lord who recounts (to me) the discourse of the Lord, Har Har. Blessed, blessed is the Guru, the Guru, the perfect True Guru, who, O Nanak, fulfils the hope held in the mind. Unite me, O Lord, with the Guru, my friend, meeting whom I may meditate on the Name of the Lord. Of the Guru, the True Guru, I would ask for talk of the Lord, and, sharing (his) fellowship, sing the Lord's virtues. Day by day, for ever, I would sing the Lord's virtues; (O Lord,) (my) mind lives on hearing your Name. O Nanak, at the moment my Master is forgotten, at that moment my soul dies. All long to see the Lord, (but) he sees (him) to whom he himself grants the sight. The one on whom my Beloved casts his glance of grace keeps the Lord, Har Har, ever cherished (in the heart). He alone cherishes the Name of the Lord, Har Har, for ever and ever, who has met my perfect True Guru. O Nanak, the servant of the Lord and the Lord have become one; by repeating the Lord, (he) has blended into the Lord. ॥6॥
562.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Most lofty is his court; (he) has no end, no near shore or far. Though one run about millions, millions, millions and hundreds of thousands of times, one does not reach his mansion, not by a sesame seed's breadth. Which is that lovely (hour), that moment, in which God is met? Hundreds of thousands of devotees worship him, hundreds of thousands of great ascetics practise nothing but austerity, hundreds of thousands of great yogis practise Yoga, hundreds of thousands of great enjoyers enjoy (his) pleasures. (O God,) you dwell in every heart, (but) few know (it). Is there some friend who would tear away the veil (between me and God)? I strive, that he may be kind (to me); to him I would give my soul in sacrifice. Wandering and wandering, I came to the Sants; (they) wiped out all my sorrow and doubt. God called (me) into his mansion, (and) I partook of the Amrit. Says Nanak, my God is lofty. ॥4॥
562.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Blessed is that moment in which the sight (of God) is beheld; I am a sacrifice to the True Guru's feet. O Giver of life, my Beloved God, (my) mind lives by remembering (your) Name, O God. Your teaching is true, (your) Bani is Amrit; O cool and soothing Being, (your) gaze discerns all. Your Hukam is true; you are seated (for ever) on the throne. My God, the Imperishable, neither comes nor goes. You are kind; we are (your) lowly servants. O Nanak, the Master fills every place and pervades all. ॥4॥
562.3: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) you are infinite; only a rare one knows (you); by the Guru's grace some (rare one) recognises (you) through the Shabad. This is (your) servant's prayer, O Beloved: may I live by meditating on your feet, O God. O merciful Being, my God, the Giver, he alone has known you to whom you give the understanding. Ever and for ever I am a sacrifice (to you); in this world and the next I look to your shelter. I, the virtueless one, have known nothing of (your) goodness; O Nanak, beholding the Saadh (the Guru), the mind is dyed (in your love). ॥4॥
563.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). That perfect God is the knower of hearts; (he) bestows the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh as (his) gift. Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek; your shelter (is mine), O all-pervading Gopal (the Lord who sustains all). (God) fills the water, the land and the sky; God dwells near; he is not far. The one on whom (he) casts his glance of grace meditates (on him), and at all hours sings the Lord's virtues. (God) cherishes all beings and creatures; Nanak has sought (his) refuge at the Lord's door. ॥4॥
563.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) you are the great Giver, the knower of hearts; O all-pervading God, my Master, you pervade all. O my Beloved God, (your) Name is (my) support; I live by hearing your Name again and again. (I have come to) your refuge, O my perfect True Guru; through the dust (of the feet) of the Sants the mind becomes pure. (Your) lotus feet I have enshrined in my heart, in (my) bosom; I am a sacrifice to the sight of you. Have mercy, that I may sing your virtues, and that Nanak may find peace repeating the Naam. ॥4॥
563.3: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) the Lord's Amrit is drunk; (then) the soul neither dies nor ever wastes away. It is by great good fortune that the perfect Guru is found; through the Guru's grace one meditates on God. The Lord (is) jewels, gems, pearls and rubies; remembering God again and again, (people) have been filled with joy. Look where I may, (it is) in the refuge of the Saadh (that) the mind is made pure by singing the Lord's virtues. My Master dwells within every heart; Nanak has received the Naam, (for) God has been pleased. ॥4॥
563.4: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Never slip from (my mind), O God, merciful to the meek; (I am in) your refuge, O all-pervading, compassionate One. Where you come to mind, that place is beautiful; the moment you are forgotten, a sigh of grief strikes. (All) beings are yours; you are ever (their) companion; give (us your) hand and pull (us) out of the world-ocean. Coming and going (birth and death) you yourself have made; the one you protect comes to no sorrow. You alone are the Master; there is no other (like you), none; Nanak makes (this) prayer with joined hands. ॥4॥
563.5: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) when you make (yourself) known, then someone knows (you), and utters the Name you have given. You are wondrous; your creation fills (one) with awe. You yourself are the cause, you yourself the creation; by (your) Hukam is birth, by (your) Hukam death. Your Name is what supports (my) mind and body; Nanak, your servant, (looks for) your grace. ॥3॥
564.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Within me is a longing to meet (him), O dear one; how shall I find the perfect Guru? Though a child be given a hundred games to play, it cannot do without milk; the hunger within me does not leave, O friend, though a hundred dishes be set before me. In my mind and body is love for the Beloved; without the sight (of him), how can the mind be at peace? Listen, my friend, my dear brother: unite me with the friend who gives peace. He knows all the pain of my soul, and daily tells (me) of the Lord. I cannot live a moment without him (God), just as the chatrik (rain-bird) cries out for water. (O God,) which of your virtues shall I recall and cherish? You keep me, the virtueless, safe. I have grown forlorn for my Husband, O friend; when shall I see that Husband with my eyes? All the enjoyment of pleasures is forgotten; without the Husband (they are) of no account. This garment gives my body no comfort; I cannot put on finery. To those friends who have enjoyed the love of the dear Beloved I bow. I put on every adornment, O friend, (but) without the Husband they were of no use. When the Husband has not asked after (me), O friend, then all (my) youth goes to waste. Blessed, blessed are those happy soul-brides, O friend, within whom the Husband abides. To those happy soul-brides, O friend, I am a sacrifice; I would ever wash their feet. So long as the delusion of another lasted, O friend, so long did I take God to be far off. When the perfect True Guru was met, O friend, then every hope and wish was fulfilled. I have found the peace above all peace, O friend; the Husband fills all. Servant Nanak has enjoyed the Lord's love, O friend, clinging to the feet of the Guru, the True Guru. ॥5॥
564.2: Raag Vadhans, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (Within me are) the true Bani, the strain of the True (Name), and reflection on the Shabad of the True One; day and night (I) praise the True One: blessed, blessed is my great fortune. O my mind, be a sacrifice to the True Name. If you remain the servant of (the Lord's) servants, you will obtain the True Name. The tongue steeped in the True One is true, and body and mind become true. Praising another than the True One, you will depart having lost your whole life. One whose farming is the True (Name), whose sowing is the True (Name), whose trade is true, earns day and night the profit of the wealth of the True Name, and (his) storehouses brim with devotion. The True (Name) for food, the True (Name) for clothing, and the Lord's Name, the True One, for support: these come to one whom (the Lord) forgives, and he finds a place in (the Lord's) mansion. They come (absorbed) in the True One and go (absorbed) in the True One, and are never cast into births again. The Gurmukhs are found true at the door of the True One, and merge in the True One. Their inner being is true, their mind is true, and true is the praise and glory (they sing); in the true place they praise the True One; I am a sacrifice to the True Guru. True (and fruitful) is that hour, true that moment, in which there is love for the True One; (then) one sees the True One, speaks the True One, and the whole visible creation is true (to him). O Nanak, only when the True One unites (one with himself) is (he) met; he himself brings (one) into union. As it pleases him, so he keeps (them); he himself gives the command. ॥8॥
565.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The mind runs about in the ten directions; how is it to sing the Lord's praises? The urge of the senses has it greatly in its grip, and lust and anger torment it every day. In Sahaj (God's) virtues are dwelt on, with praise, Waah Waah; the Name of Ram is hard to come by in this age; through the Guru's teaching the Lord's essence is drunk. When, recognising the Shabad, the mind becomes pure, then it sings the Lord's praises. When through the Guru's teaching one recognises one's own self, then one finds a dwelling in one's own home (within). O my mind, ever steeped in (his) love, sing the Lord's praises for ever. The Lord is pure, ever the giver of peace; obtain (from him) the fruit your mind longs for. We, the lowly, have become exalted in the Lord's refuge. He has pulled out the sinking stone; true is his glory. From poison (we) have become Amrit, having gained understanding through the Guru's teaching. From the akk (a bitter wild shrub) we have become fragrant sandal; fragrance has been made to dwell within. Human birth is hard to come by; coming into the world, (that one alone) has earned (the profit) who by perfect fortune meets the True Guru and meditates on the Lord's Name. The manmukhs, gone astray, cling to poison, and have wasted this precious life. The Lord's Name is ever an ocean of peace, (yet) the true Shabad has not pleased them. With the mouth everyone says Har Har; rare is the one who has enshrined (him) in the heart. O Nanak, those in whose hearts (the Lord) has come to dwell have attained liberation and release. ॥8॥
565.2: Raag Vadhans, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Having defiled the body with falsehood, why bathe (at places of pilgrimage)? That one alone is accepted as bathed, when truth is practised. When truth is within, one becomes true; then the True One is found. Without what (God) has written there is no understanding; by talking and talking (life) is lost. Wherever one goes to sit, one should speak what is good, and have the Shabad inscribed in one's consciousness. Having defiled the body with falsehood, why bathe (at places of pilgrimage)? I spoke the word (of your praise) only when you made me speak it. The Amrit Name of the Lord has become dear to my mind. The Name has come to taste sweet to the mind, and pain has pulled down its camp. Peace came to dwell in the mind when you gave the command. The glance of grace is yours, the prayer is mine, O you who brought yourself into being. I spoke the word (of your praise) only when you made me speak it. The Master grants each his turn (of life) by the deeds he has done. Call no one bad, and do not start a quarrel. Pick no quarrel with the Master; (so) you only bring ruin on yourself. Having made a rival of the One whose company you must keep, what use is it to go (to him) and weep? What he gives is to be borne; (what you would say) is to be said to your own mind, not voiced aloud in complaint. The Master grants each his turn (of life) by the deeds he has done. He himself has created all, and he himself casts his glance of grace. No one asks for the bitter; all ask for the sweet. Let everyone ask for the sweet and see: the Master does what pleases him. Acts of merit, gifts in charity, many deeds: none of it is equal to the Name, or matches it. O Nanak, those who have received the Name were shown grace long ago, from the very beginning. He himself has created all, and he himself casts his glance of grace. ॥4॥
566.1: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (O Lord,) show mercy, that I may utter your Name. You yourself have created all, and you yourself pervade all. You yourself pervade all; having created (beings), you have set them to their toil. Some you yourself have made kings; others you have sent wandering to beg. Greed and attachment you have made sweet; in this delusion (the world) has gone astray. Show your mercy always; only then can I utter the Name. Your Name is true, and is ever dear to my mind. Pain has gone, and peace has come to dwell (in me). Gods and men, the refined and the wise, sing (of you); gods and men, the refined and the wise, those who are pleasing to your mind, sing (of you). Bewitched by Maya, (others) do not remember (you), and waste this precious life. Some, dull and foolish, never remember (you) at all; whoever has come must go. Your Name is ever true; it alone is dear to my mind. Lovely is your hour (when you are remembered); your Bani is Amrit. (Your) servants serve (you) with love; those mortals have come to know the taste (of the Name). Those mortals alone have come to know the taste who have received the Amrit. Those who are steeped in your Name rise higher every day. Not one rite, religious duty or discipline (avails), so long as I do not recognise the One. Ever lovely is your hour (when you are remembered); your Bani is Amrit. I am a sacrifice to (your) True Name. Your rule never passes away. Your rule is ever unshakeable; it never passes away. He alone is your servant who stays merged in Sahaj. No enemy, no pain touches him at all, and sin does not come near. May I ever be a sacrifice to your one Name. In age after age (there have been) your devotees, who sing your praise, O Master, at your door, and repeat (the Name of) the one True Murari (the Lord). They repeat (the Name of) the True Murari only when you make (it) dwell in their minds; doubt and delusion are of your making, (and they repeat it) when you take this away. By the Guru's grace show (us) mercy, and save (us) from Jam. In age after age (there have been) your devotees. O my great Master, unseen and infinite, how am I to make my prayer (to you)? I do not know how to speak. If you cast your glance of grace, then I recognise the True One. I recognise your Truth only when you yourself give understanding; you have made pain and hunger in the world, and (you) take this dread away. Nanak prays: dread goes when one understands through reflection on the Guru's word. He himself is the great Master, unseen and infinite. Your eyes are beautiful, your teeth delightful; lovely is your nose, and long your hair. (Your) body is golden, cast in gold. Cast in gold, (wearing) Krishna's garland: meditate (on him), O friends. (So that) you need not stand at Jam's door, hear this counsel, O brides. The heron of herons becomes the swan of swans, (when) the scum of the mind comes off. (Your) eyes are beautiful, (your) teeth delightful. Lovely is your gait, sweet your speech. (It is as) the koels' cooing; lively is (your) youth. Lively youth is pleasing to you yourself; the wish of (your own) mind is fulfilled. Like an elephant (saarang) he sets down his foot with a stately sway, rapt in himself. She who is steeped in Sri Rang (the Lord of Lakshmi) moves about rapt, like the waters of the Ganga. Nanak, the Lord's servant, prays: lovely is your gait, sweet your speech. ॥8॥

Krishna's garland (ਕ੍ਰਿਸਨ ਮਾਲਾ): the garland of forest flowers (Vaijayanti) that Krishna wears. The heron, standing still as if in meditation while it watches for fish, is the image of the hypocrite; the swan, of the pure soul.
567.1: Raag Vadhans, Chhants, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Steeped in the love of your own Husband, dear one, you are a bride full of glory; you stay merged in the true Shabad, dear one, and for (your) love and affection the Husband delights in you. Dear (to him) for her true love, adorned by her Husband, she has formed a bond of love with the Lord, Har Har. When she shed her self-conceit, then she found the Husband, and merged in the Guru's Shabad. That soul-bride, made beautiful by the Shabad, is drawn by love; within her is a dear affection. O Nanak, the Husband himself has united that soul-bride (with himself); the True King has adorned her. O bride without virtue, see the Husband present before you. For those who through the Guru have enjoyed (his) love, dear one, the Husband pervades all, filling everything. The Husband pervades all, filling everything: see him present before you; in every age the One alone is known. The bride, young and innocent, enjoys the Husband's love in Sahaj; she has met the One who shapes (each) by their deeds. She who has tasted the Lord's essence, and through the Shabad has sung (his praise) well, abides wholly in the Lord's pool. O Nanak, that bride pleases the Husband who, through the Shabad, stays in his presence. Go, dear one, and ask the happy soul-brides who have shed their self-conceit from within. Those who have not shed their self-conceit from within, dear one, have not grasped the Husband's Hukam. Those who have shed their self-conceit have found the Husband; (each) enjoys delight in his love. Ever steeped in (his) love, rapt in Sahaj, she utters the Name day and night. Fortunate is that bride: her attention is fixed (on him) within, and the Lord's love has become dear to her. O Nanak, the bride who has made truth her adornment is steeped (in his love) in Sahaj. Subdue your Haumai, dear one, and walk in the Guru's will. (So) you will ever enjoy the love of the Lord, your Husband, dear one, finding a dwelling in your own home (within). Finding a dwelling in her own home, she makes the Shabad resound, and is a wife happy in her Husband for ever. The Husband is full of delight, his youth ever fresh; day and night the Husband keeps her adorned. The Lord, her Husband, is her wedded bliss; good fortune is on her forehead; the true Shabad makes her beautiful. O Nanak, the bride is steeped in the Lord's love when she walks in the True Guru's will. ॥4॥
Ram at the end of many lines of these Chhants is a sung word of the measure, a calling on the Lord; it is not rendered.
Muiye (literally, O dead one) is a Punjabi word with which women address one another, here fondly; it is rendered dear one.
568.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through the Guru, all trade is good, if it is done in Sahaj. Let the Name be uttered day and night, and the Lord's essence drunk: (this is) the profit. The Lord's essence is taken as the profit, the Lord is enjoyed, (when one) utters the Name day and night; as he gathers virtues, (his) faults are sold off, and he comes to know his own self. Through the Guru's teaching great glory has been gained; through the true Shabad the essence (of the Name) is drunk. O Nanak, devotion to the Lord is wondrous; rare is the one who, through the Guru, performs it. Through the Guru, let the crop of the Lord be sown within, and let the Lord be made to sprout in the body. Within your own home, savour the essence, and earn the profit for the world beyond. The one who enshrines the Lord in his mind (earns) the profit for the world beyond; blessed is (such) farming and trade. He meditates on the Lord's Name, enshrines it in his mind, and understands through reflection on the Guru's word. The manmukhs have worn themselves out farming and trading, (yet) their craving and hunger do not go. Says Nanak: sow the Name within the mind, with love, through the true Shabad. They alone take up the Lord's trade on whose forehead is the jewel of great fortune. Through the Guru's teaching (their) mind has come to dwell in its own home, and through the true Shabad (comes) detachment. Good fortune is on their face and forehead; their detachment is in the True One; steeped in the True One, they are given to reflection. Without the Name the whole world is crazed; (they) have subdued Haumai through the Shabad. Attached to the true Shabad, wisdom wells up; through the Guru the Name is (their) wedded bliss. O Nanak, through the Shabad the destroyer of fear is met; one with good fortune on the forehead enjoys the Lord. Farming and trade are all (his) Hukam; in accepting the Hukam lies glory. Through the Guru's teaching the Hukam is understood; by the Hukam (he) unites (one) in union (with himself). United by the Hukam, (one) merges in Sahaj; the Guru's Shabad is infinite. True glory is gained from the Guru; the True One is the one who adorns. The destroyer of fear is found when self-conceit is shed; through the Guru (he) unites (one) in union. Says Nanak: the Name of the Immaculate One, inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses, pervades all by (his) Hukam. ॥4॥
569.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O my mind, ever keep the True One cherished (in your heart). (So) you will dwell in peace in your own home (within), and Jamkaal (death) cannot touch you. Death, its net and Jam cannot so much as look at one who fixes his attention on the true Shabad; ever steeped in the True One, (his) mind is pure, and (his) coming and going comes to an end. In the love of another and in doubt the manmukh (world) is ruined, held fast in attachment by Jamkaal. Says Nanak: listen, O my mind, ever keep the True One cherished (in your heart). O my mind, within you is the treasure; do not seek the thing outside. Take for your food whatever pleases (God), and through the Guru behold with (inner) sight. Through the Guru behold with (inner) sight, O my mind: within (you) is the Lord's Name, your friend. The manmukhs are blind, empty of (spiritual) wisdom; in the love of another they are led astray. Without the Name no one is set free; all (the world) is bound by Jamkaal. Says Nanak: within you is the treasure; do not seek the thing outside. O my mind, having obtained the precious gift of (human) birth, some have taken up the trade in the True One; they serve their own True Guru, and within (them) is the Shabad of the Infinite. Within (them) is the Shabad of the Infinite, and the Lord's Name is dear (to them); in the Name itself they have obtained the nine treasures. The manmukhs are caught in attachment to Maya and tormented by pain; in (the love of) another they have lost their honour. (Those who,) subduing Haumai, merge in the true Shabad are steeped deeply in the True One. O Nanak, a human birth is hard to come by; the True Guru has given (them) this understanding. O my mind, those who serve their own True Guru are people of great good fortune. Those who subdue their own mind are the detached. Those people are detached, their attention fixed on the True One; they have recognised their own self. Their understanding is steady and most deeply dyed; through the Guru, in Sahaj, they have uttered the Name. Some are devoted to women and in love with attachment to Maya; (such) unfortunate manmukhs remain asleep. O Nanak, those who serve their own Guru in Sahaj are fortunate in full measure. ॥4॥
The nine treasures (nidhis): by tradition, the nine treasures of Kuber, the god of wealth; that is, all the riches of the world.
569.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Priceless jewels are traded (by those to whom) the True Guru has given understanding; (Their) profit and gain is devotion to the Lord; in (his) virtues (they) merge in the Lord of virtues. He to whom (God) himself gives understanding merges, in (his) virtues, in the Lord of virtues; in the world (he earns) the profit of devotion. Without devotion there is no peace, and in (the love of) another honour is lost; through the Guru's teaching (he makes) the Name his support. The merchandise of the Name is gain for ever (to him) whom (God) sets to this trade. Priceless jewels are traded when the True Guru gives understanding. Attachment to Maya is pain, all of it; this trade is false. Speaking falsehood, poison is eaten, and the vices grow many. The vices grow many, this world is (all) anxiety, and without the Name honour is lost. Reading and reading, the pandits expound their disputes; without understanding there is no peace. (Their) coming and going never ends; attachment to Maya is dear (to them). Attachment to Maya is pain, all of it; this trade is false. The false and the genuine are all tested in that court of the True One. The false are thrown out of the Lord's court; standing, they cry out. Standing, they cry out, the foolish and the ignorant, who as manmukhs have wasted their life. Maya, the poison that has led the world astray, (so beguiled them that) the True Name did not please (them). Bearing enmity towards the Sants, the manmukh world earns pain. The false and the genuine are tested in that true court. (God) himself does (all); to whom else should one speak? Nothing else can be done. To whatever (task) pleases him he will set (each one), as befits his greatness. As befits his greatness, he himself causes (all) to be done; no one is (of himself) a hero, and no one a weakling. The Life of the world, the Giver, the Maker (of beings) according to (their) deeds: he himself forgives. By the Guru's grace self-conceit is shed; O Nanak, through the Name honour is gained. (God) himself does (all); to whom else should one speak? Nothing else can be done. ॥4॥
570.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Lord's Name is the true merchandise, the true trade. Through the Guru's teaching the Lord's Name is traded; its price is exceedingly great. Exceedingly great is the worth of the trade in Truth; the fortunate have taken up this true trade. Within and without they are steeped in devotion, their attention fixed on the True Name. He alone on whom (God) casts his glance of grace finds the True One, reflecting through the Guru's Shabad. O Nanak, those steeped in the Name, they alone have found peace in the trade of the True One. Haumai and Maya are filth; (the mind) is smeared with the filth of Maya. Through the Guru's teaching the mind is pure; with the tongue one should drink the Lord's sweet essence. With the tongue one should drink the Lord's sweet essence; (then) the heart is drenched, and through the true Shabad it comes to reflect. Within is a little well, full of Amrit; through the Shabad the water-drawer (the attention) draws (from it) and drinks. He alone on whom (God) casts his glance of grace is joined to the True One; with the tongue one should remember the Lord. O Nanak, those steeped in the Name are pure; the rest are smeared with the filth of Haumai. The pandits and the astrologers, all of them, read and read and shout aloud; to whom are they crying out? Within (them) is attachment to Maya, and filth clings (to them); (theirs) are the dealings of Maya. The dealings of Maya are dear to the world; in coming and going it suffers pain. The worm of poison clings to poison, and is sunk in filth. What is written from the start, that alone (a being) acts out; there is no one to erase it. O Nanak, those steeped in the Name have found peace for ever; the other fools, the ignorant, have died shouting. The mind is dyed in attachment to Maya; in attachment (it) has no awareness at all. If through the Guru this mind is dyed, the colour of another departs. The colour of another departs, (the mind) merges in the True One, and (its) storehouses are filled with Truth. He alone who becomes Gurmukh understands (this); the Adorner adorns (him) with Truth. He whom (God) himself unites, he meets the Lord; nothing more can be said. O Nanak, without the Name (the world) is led astray in doubt; some, having taken on (his) love, are steeped in the Name. ॥4॥
571.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O my mind, the world is a coming and going; in the end, release is in the True One. (When) the True One himself forgives, then there is no further round (of birth and death). Then there is no further round; in the end, release is in the True One; through the Guru, glory is received. Steeped in the love of the True One, rapt in Sahaj, they remain absorbed in Sahaj. The True One has become pleasing to their mind, and they have enshrined the True One; steeped in the Shabad, in the end they find release. O Nanak, those steeped in the Name merge in the True One; never again (do they make) a round in the world-ocean. Attachment to Maya is madness, all of it; in the love of another (the world) is led astray. Mother, father: all of it is attachment; (the world) is entangled in attachment itself. It is entangled in attachment by what it earned before; no one can erase that. He who fashioned the creation, having made it, watches over it; there is no other as great as he. The blind manmukh burns and burns and wastes away; without the Shabad, peace has not come (to him). O Nanak, without the Name everyone has gone wrong; in attachment to Maya (the world) is led astray. Seeing this world burning, (I) have run to the Lord's refuge. I offer a prayer before the perfect Guru: save (me), grant (me) glory. Keep (me) in your refuge, (grant me) the glory of the Lord's Name; no other giver is your equal. Those set to (your) service are of great good fortune; they have known the One (who is) in every age. (One may) practise continence, truthfulness, self-restraint and (such) deeds, (but) without the Guru the (high) state of liberation is not attained. O Nanak, (God) gives understanding of the Shabad to him who goes and falls into the Lord's refuge. The understanding the Lord gives, that alone wells up; there is no other understanding. Within and without, you alone are; you yourself give understanding. You yourself give understanding, and no other (understanding) pleases; through the Guru (the soul) has tasted the Lord's sweet essence. At the True One's door he is ever true who has sung (his) praise through the true Shabad. Within the home (of his heart) he has found his own true home; the True Guru gives (him) glory. O Nanak, those who are steeped in the Name, they alone reach (the Lord's) mansion; that understanding (of theirs) is approved by the True One. ॥4॥
572.1: Raag Vadhans, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. In my mind, in my mind, the True Guru has instilled love. He has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Har Har, dwell in my mind. He has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, dwell in my mind, (the Name) that takes away all pains. By great good fortune (I) have had the sight of the Guru; blessed, blessed is my True Guru. Rising and sitting, (I) serve the True Guru, by serving whom peace has been found. In my mind, in my mind, love for the True Guru has been instilled. I live, I live: seeing the True Guru, (my mind) is filled with delight. (The Guru) implants the Lord's Name, the Lord's Name (in me); repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (my mind) blossoms. Repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the lotus (of the heart) has bloomed; (I) have obtained the Lord's Name, the nine treasures. The sickness of Haumai has gone and the pain has lifted; in Sahaj, (my) Samadhi (deep absorption) is fixed on the Lord. From the True Guru (I) have obtained the glory of the Lord's Name; touching (the feet of) the divine True Guru, the mind has found peace. I live, I live: seeing the True Guru, (my mind) is filled with delight. Should someone bring (him), someone bring and unite (me with) my perfect True Guru, (then) I would give my mind and body, my mind and body to him, cutting up my body (for him). My mind and body, cut piece by piece, I would give to him who lets me hear the True Guru's words. Bairag (longing for the Lord) has arisen in my mind; the longing (mind), meeting the Guru, finds peace in the sight of him. O Lord, Har Har, giver of peace, show mercy: give me the dust of the True Guru's feet. Should someone bring (him), someone bring and unite (me with) my perfect True Guru! For me there is no other giver equal to the Guru, equal to the Guru. (The Guru) gives the gift of the Lord, the gift of the Lord, who is the Purakh, the all-pervading Being, Niranjan (free of the stain of Maya). Those who have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har: their pain, doubt and fear have fled. In the spirit of a servant, the fortunate ones whose minds are fixed on the Guru's feet have met (the Lord). Says Nanak: the Lord himself unites (them); meeting the True Guru, the Purakh, there is peace. For me there is no other giver equal to the Guru, equal to the Guru. ॥4॥
572.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Without the Guru I, without the Guru I am utterly without honour. The world's Life, the world's Life, the Giver: through union with the Guru I have merged (in him). The True Guru united (me), and I merged in the Lord's Name; repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, I have meditated (on him). He for whom I went searching and searching, that Friend, the Lord, I have found in (my own) home. With an undivided gaze I have known the Lord as the One; I have recognised the Lord who pervades every soul (Atam Ram). Without the Guru I, without the Guru I am utterly without honour. Those who have found the True Guru, who have found the True Guru, the Lord God brings into union (with himself). Their feet, their feet I serve; I cling to their feet. O Lord, Har Har, I serve the feet of those who have meditated on the True Guru, the Purakh, on God. You are the great Giver, the knower of hearts; fulfil my longing, O Lord, my King. In union with the Gursikhs my longing is fulfilled, and night and day (I) sing the Lord's praises. Those who have found the True Guru, who have found the True Guru, the Lord God brings into union (with himself). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the Gursikh, my beloved friend, who lets me hear the Lord's Name, the Lord's Name; the Name is my Beloved, (my) mainstay. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the friend of my life-breath; without it I do not live for a moment, not for the blink of an eye. (If) the Lord, Har Har, the giver of peace, shows mercy, (then) through the Guru I drink the Amrit. The Lord himself instils the longing and unites (the soul with himself); the Lord himself, of himself, adorns (it). I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the Gursikh, my beloved friend. The Lord himself, the Lord himself is that Purakh, Niranjan. The Lord himself, the Lord himself unites (the soul with himself); what he does, that comes to be. What pleases the Lord God, that alone comes to be; nothing else can be done. By great cleverness (he) cannot be won; all have tried their cleverness and grown weary. By the Guru's grace servant Nanak has seen (him): for me there is none other than the Lord. The Lord himself, the Lord himself is that Purakh, Niranjan. ॥4॥
573.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Lord, unite me with the True Guru, with the True Guru; O Lord, the True Guru's feet are dear to me. The darkness of ignorance is gone, for the Guru has put the salve of the Guru's wisdom (in my eyes). The True Guru has applied the salve of the Guru's wisdom, and the darkness of ignorance has been destroyed. By serving the True Guru I have reached the highest state; I have repeated (the Name of) the Lord with each breath and each mouthful. Those to whom the Lord God has shown grace, he has joined to the True Guru's service. O Lord, unite me with the True Guru, with the True Guru; O Lord, the True Guru's feet are dear to me. My True Guru, my True Guru is dear (to me); I cannot live without the Guru. He gives (me) the Lord's Name, the Lord's Name, my companion at the last. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is my companion at the last; the Guru, the True Guru, has made the Name firm (within me). Where no son, no wife, no friend (stands by), there the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has set (me) free. Blessed, blessed is the True Guru, the Purakh, Niranjan, meeting whom I meditate on the Lord's Name. My True Guru, my True Guru is dear (to me); I cannot live without the Guru. Those who have not gained the sight, the sight of the True Guru, the Purakh, fruitless, fruitless is their life; they have wasted it all in vain. They have wasted their life for nothing; those Saakats (who have turned from God) are dead, and dying, they pine. Though the jewel, the precious thing, is in their own home, they go hungry; those luckless ones are far from the Lord. For the Lord's sake, never look upon those who have not meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, those who have not gained the sight, the sight of the True Guru, the Purakh. I am a humble chatrik, a chatrik; this is my prayer to the Lord: unite me with the Guru, my Beloved, so that, meeting the Guru, I may worship the True Guru. I can worship the True Guru and the Lord, Har Har, (only) when the Lord God shows grace. I have no friend other than the Guru; the Guru, the True Guru, is my life itself. Says Nanak, within me the Guru has made the Naam firm: the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the ever-true Lord. I am a humble chatrik, a chatrik; (this) is my prayer to the Lord. ॥4॥
574.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). O Lord, show grace, show grace: unite (me) with the True Guru, the giver of peace. I would ask, I would ask the True Guru about the Lord. I would ask the True Guru about the Lord, (the Guru) who has gained the treasure of the Naam. I would fall at (his) feet and pray to (him) every day; the Guru, the True Guru, has shown the way. He alone is a devotee who knows pain and pleasure as one and the same, and is steeped in the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in the Lord. O Lord, show grace, show grace: unite (me) with the Guru, the True Guru, the giver of peace. Listen through the Guru, listen through the Guru: by the Name, Haumai and all sins are destroyed. Repeat the Lord, Har Har, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: (by it) the fevers of the world have come off. Those who have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have had their pains and sins taken away. The True Guru has put the sword of wisdom in (their) hand, and (with it) they have struck down and destroyed Jam's servants. The Lord God, the giver of peace, has shown grace, and pains, sins and torments have gone. Listen to the Name through the Guru, listen through the Guru: Haumai and all sins are destroyed. Repeat the Lord, Har Har, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: (that Name) has become dear to my mind. Repeating (it) with the mouth through the Guru, with the mouth through the Guru, (one) has driven out all ailments. Repeating (it) through the Guru, (one) has driven out all ailments, and the body has become whole. Night and day the Samadhi of Sahaj stays fixed on the Lord, for (one) has repeated the Lord, the deep and profound. Whoever has meditated on the Naam, of (high) caste or of no caste, has gained the supreme treasure. Repeat the Lord, Har Har, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: (that Name) has become dear to my mind. Show grace, O Lord, show grace, O Lord; in your grace, save (me). I am a sinner, I am a sinner, without virtue, lowly, (but) yours. I, a sinner, without virtue, lowly, (but) yours, have come to your refuge, O merciful Lord. You are the breaker of sorrows, the giver of all peace; I, a stone, have crossed over, ferried across by you. Meeting the True Guru, (I) have found the savour of the Lord; the Name has saved servant Nanak. Show grace, O Lord, show grace, O Lord; in your grace, save (me). ॥4॥
575.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghorian, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. This body is a fine mare, dear ones, created by the Lord. Blessed is the human birth; (this body) is gained through merit. The human birth is gained through great merit; that body is golden and lovely, which, through the Guru, takes on the deep crimson dye, dyed afresh with the Lord, Har Har Har. This body is beautiful, for through it I repeat the Lord; it is made lovely by the Name of the Lord, Har Har. (This body) is gained by great good fortune, with the Naam for companion; O servant Nanak, it is the Lord who created it. Understanding the Good One, I put the saddle on the body; mounting it, dear ones, I cross the treacherous (world-) ocean. That treacherous ocean has endless waves; through the Guru, (the Lord) carries (one) across. Boarding the ship of the Lord, the fortunate one crosses over; the Guru, the boatman, carries (him) across through the Shabad. Night and day, in the Lord's love, he sings the Lord's virtues; dyed with the Lord, he becomes of the Lord's own colour. Servant Nanak has attained the state of nirvana, where desire is stilled: the Lord's state, sublime and good. The bridle in (the mare's) mouth is the wisdom the Guru has made firm (within); the Lord's love within the body is the whip laid on it. Laying on the whip of love for the Lord, Har Har, within the body, (one) conquers the mind; through the Guru (alone) is it conquered. He shapes the unshaped (mind), receives the Shabad, and drinks the Amrit, the Lord's essence. Hearing with his ears the Bani the Guru has uttered, he has put the Lord's colour on the mare. The road is long, the path is hard; (the Guru) has brought servant Nanak across it. The body is a mare, a fine mare, created by the Lord. Blessed, blessed is that mare through which (one) repeats the Lord God. That (mare) through which (one) repeats the Lord God is blessed and worthy of praise; it is gained as ordained from the first, by the deeds (of the past) gathered together. Mount the dear body-mare that carries (you) over the treacherous (ocean), and through the Guru meet the Lord of supreme bliss. The perfect Lord, Har Har, has arranged the wedding; the Sants have gathered, and the wedding party has come. Servant Nanak has found the Lord as the Groom; there is rejoicing, and the Sants, gathered together, offer their congratulations. ॥4॥
Ghorian: the wedding songs that the groom's sisters and the women of the house sing as he mounts the mare to ride out for his wedding; in these two chhants the human body is the mare.
575.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). This body is a lovely mare, dyed in a new colour by the Lord. It has begged the Guru for the Guru's wisdom, the wisdom of the Lord. It begged for wisdom, for the Lord's beautiful discourse, for the Lord's Name, and came to know (his) state and measure. The Creator has made its whole life fruitful; joined to the Name of the Lord, Ram, it has spoken (of him). Praising the Name of the Lord, Ram, the Lord's servants have begged the Lord God for the Lord's devotion. Servant Nanak says: listen, O Sants, devotion to the Lord, Govind, is what is good. The body (-mare) is golden, its saddle of gold, studded with the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as its jewel. Setting (in it) the jewel of the Name, (one) has found Govind; the Lord is met, and with him the Lord's virtues and peace in plenty. Whoever has received the Guru's Shabad and meditated on the Lord's Name is, by great fortune, coloured with the Lord's colour. He has met the Lord, the Master, the knower of hearts, the Lord ever new, ever fresh in colour. Nanak utters (the Name) and knows the Name; he has begged the Lord God for the Lord's Name. The Guru has put the bridle in (the mare's) mouth and set the elephant-goad (on the mind); the elephant of the mind has come under control through the Guru's Shabad. The mind has come under control, the supreme state is reached, and that soul-bride is loved by her Husband. Within her, love for the Lord has taken hold; the wife of the Lord God shines in his home. Dyed in the Lord's love, rapt in Sahaj, she has found the Lord God, Har Har. Servant Nanak, the slave of the Lord, says: (only) the fortunate have meditated on the Lord, Har Har. The body is the mare, dear ones, through which the Lord is found. Meeting the True Guru, dear ones, (one) has sung the song of joy. Singing the Lord's song of joy, the Name of Ram, the servant serves the Lord with a servant's devotion; he goes and reaches God's palace of joy, and enjoys the delight of the Lord's love. He sings the virtues of Ram with love in his mind, and, following the Guru's teaching, meditates on the Lord in his mind. The Lord has shown grace to servant Nanak: mounting the body-mare, he has found the Lord. ॥4॥
576.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 4, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Meeting the Guru, dear ones, I have found the dear Lord. I have given (him) this body and mind, offering them up again and again. Giving body and mind, I have won over the world-ocean; my subjection to Jam is ended. I have become steady, I have drunk the Amrit, and (my) coming and going has stopped. I have found that home and merged in Sahaj; the Lord's Name is (my) support. Says Nanak, in peace I enjoy delights; I bow to the perfect Guru. Listen, my dear friend, my companion: the Guru has given (me) the mantra, the true Shabad. I have meditated on the true Shabad and sung the song of joy, and the anxieties have left my mind. I have found that God; (now I) go nowhere else, and ever, ever abide with (him). Whoever is pleasing to dear God has true honour; God has given him the wealth of the Lord, in Sahaj. Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that servant; (O God,) through him all have received your gift. When it pleased you, (O God,) then (we) were satisfied and filled. The mind has become cool; all thirst is quenched. The mind has become cool, the burning (within) is ended, and a great treasure is found. All the Sikhs and servants have begun to partake (of it); I am a sacrifice to the True Guru. They have become fearless, dyed in the Master's love, and have put out the fear of Jam. Nanak is (your) slave, (your) servant ever at (your) side; may I worship you with (my) attention fixed (on you). (My) hopes and desires are fulfilled, O my dear (Lord). I am without virtue, dear (Lord); all virtues are yours. All virtues are yours, my Master; with what mouth shall I praise you? You weighed none of my merits or faults; you forgave me in a moment. The nine treasures are mine; congratulations ring out, and the unstruck trumpets play. Says Nanak, I have found the Husband in my own home; all my sorrows, dear (Lord), have left me. ॥4॥
The unstruck (Anhad) trumpets: the divine music, made by no striking, that sounds unbroken within.
577.1: What use is listening to falsehood? (False things) go by like gusts of the wind. O Nanak, accepted are those ears that hear the True Master. I am a sacrifice through and through to those who have heard God with their ears. They are at peace in Sahaj who have uttered (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, with the tongue. They are at peace in Sahaj, priceless in virtue; they have come to carry the world across. God's feet are the ship across the ocean of fear; (through them) they have carried countless ones across. Those on whom my Master has shown grace — their account has not been reckoned. Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice through and through to the one who has heard God with his ears. With my eyes I have seen the world, but the thirst is not quenched; it is great in me. O Nanak, those eyes are of another kind, which see my Beloved. I am a sacrifice to those who have beheld the Lord God. They are pleasing in the Lord's true court. Honoured by the Master, they are foremost, steeped in love for the Lord. Filled with the Lord's essence, merged in Sahaj, they know the all-pervading Lord in every heart. They alone are true friends, they are Sants, they are at peace, who are pleasing to their Master. Says Nanak, to those who have beheld the Lord God I am ever a sacrifice. Without the Name, the body is in darkness, blind and empty. O Nanak, his life bears fruit in whose heart the True Master has come to dwell. I am cut in pieces as a sacrifice to those who have beheld my Lord God. The Lord's servants have tasted the sweet Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, and are fulfilled. The Lord is sweet to their minds; God is pleased, the Amrit has rained down, and there is peace. Sorrow is destroyed and delusion banished from the body by hailing the victory of the Master, the Lord of the world. They are free of attachment, (their) vices have ceased, and their tie with the five (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) is broken. Says Nanak, I am cut in pieces as a sacrifice to those in whose heart my Lord God has come to dwell. Those whom the Lord wants are alone called (his) servants. Nanak knows it to be true: the Master is not apart from the Sants. Water meets water and is blended in; (the soul's) light has merged with the Light (of God). The perfect Purakh, the Creator, has taken (it) into himself; he alone, he himself, is known (everywhere). There, in Sunn (the stillness where no thought stirs) and in Sahaj, Samadhi holds, and the One, the One alone, is spoken of. He himself is hidden, he himself is unbound; he himself tells of himself. O Nanak, delusion, fear and the (three) qualities (of Maya) are destroyed; water meets water and is blended in. ॥4॥
578.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O God, Cause of creation, all-powerful, protect the whole world, giving (it) your hand. All-powerful Master, able to shelter those who seek refuge, treasure of mercy, giver of peace, To your servants who have recognised the One, I am a sacrifice. (Your) colour and sign cannot be perceived; you are beyond all telling. Nanak prays: hear (my) prayer, O God, Cause of creation, all-powerful. These beings are yours; you are (their) Creator. O God, you take away pain, suffering and doubt. Taking away doubt, pain and suffering in an instant, save (us), O God, merciful to the meek. (You are) mother, father, master and friend; the whole world is your child, O Gopal. Whoever comes to (your) refuge obtains the treasure of virtues; he is not born again and does not die. Nanak, your servant, prays: all beings are yours; you are (their) Creator. At all hours the Lord is to be meditated on; (so) the fruit the mind longs for is obtained. Meditating on God, the mind's desire is obtained, and the terrors of Jam are erased. (One who) has sung of Gobind in the Saadh Sangat has had (his) hope fulfilled. Giving up pride, attachment and all vices, one becomes pleasing to God's mind. Nanak prays: day and night, the Lord, Har Har, is ever to be meditated on. At (his) door the unstruck music plays; in every heart the Lord Gobind resounds. Govind resounds, ever abiding (there), beyond reach, beyond the senses, lofty. His virtues are endless; nothing can be said (of them), and no one can reach (him). He himself creates, he himself sustains; he has fashioned all beings and creatures. Nanak prays: there is peace in the Naam and in devotion; at (his) door the unstruck music plays. ॥4॥
578.2: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 5, Alahniyan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Blessed is the Creator, the True King, who has set the world to its worldly business. When the allotted time is up and the cup is full, the dear one is seized and driven off. The dear one is seized and driven off when the written (order) comes, and all the brothers weep. Body and swan (the soul) are parted when the days are run out, O my mother. As was written, so has (each) received, according to what (each) earned before. Blessed is the Creator, the True King, who has set the world to its worldly business. Remember the Master, O my brothers; all must make this journey. Here the false business (of the world) lasts four days; (all) must surely go on ahead. (All) must surely go on ahead, like guests; why should we be proud? Let us take the Name of him alone, by serving whom peace is found in (his) court. Ahead, no one's command holds at all; on each head falls what (each) has done. Remember the Master, O my brothers; all must make this journey. Whatever pleases the all-powerful (Lord), that comes to pass; this world is (but) a pretext. The True Creator pervades the water, the land and the sky. The True Creator is unseen and infinite; his limit has not been found. Fruitful is the coming (into the world) of those who have meditated (on him) with a single mind. He himself tears down, and tearing down builds again; by (his) Hukam he sets (all) right. Whatever pleases the all-powerful (Lord), that comes to pass; this world is (but) a pretext. Says Nanak: O brother, that one is known to weep (truly) who weeps with love (for the Lord). O brother, if one weeps for the sake of worldly goods, all that weeping is in vain. All that weeping is in vain; the heedless world weeps for the sake of Maya. It discerns nothing of good and bad, and wastes this body for nothing. Everyone who has come here shall go; (yet) you act in pride over what is false. Says Nanak: O brother, that one is known to weep (truly) who weeps with love (for the Lord). ॥4॥

Alahniyan: the dirges women sing together over the dead, praising the departed and beating their breasts in time. In their measure the Guru teaches acceptance of the Lord's will and his praise in place of wailing.
The cup (paai): the bowl of a water-clock, with a small hole in its bottom; floating on water it slowly fills and sinks. The full cup is the measure of a life run out.
579.1: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Come, my friends, let us meet and take the True Name. Let us weep over the parting of the body, (and) keep our Master in mind. Let us keep the Master in mind and watch the road (ahead): we too must go there. He whose (creature) it was has taken (it back); his will has come to pass. What (the departed one) did and gathered has come before (him); what command can we give? Come, my friends, let us meet and take the True Name. Death should not be called bad, O people, if one knows how to die such a death. Serve your all-powerful Master, (so that) the road ahead becomes easy. If you go by the easy road, you will gain the fruit, and ahead you will receive glory. If you go with the offering (of the Name) and merge in the True One, your honour will be accepted at the reckoning. You will gain a place in the (Lord's) mansion and be pleasing to the Master; (such a one) enjoys delights in his love. Death should not be called bad, O people, if anyone knows how to die. The death of brave men is rightful, if they die approved (by the Lord). Only those are called brave ahead who are given true honour in (the Lord's) court. In the court they receive honour, they depart with honour, and ahead no pain touches them. If they meditate (on him) as the One, they gain the fruit; serving him, fear runs away. Do not speak proud words; keep within your own mind: the Knower himself knows (all). The death of brave men is rightful, if they die approved (by the Lord). Says Nanak: for whom, O brother, should one weep? This world is a play. The Master watches over what he has made, and gives thought to (his) creation. He gives thought to (his) creation and gives (it) support; he who made it knows (it). He himself sees, he himself understands, he himself recognises (his) Hukam. He who made all (this) alone knows (it); his form is infinite. Says Nanak: for whom, O brother, should one weep? This world is a play. ॥4॥
580.1: Raag Vadhans Dakhani, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Know the Creator to be true, the eternal; the True One is the Sustainer, who fashioned his own self by himself, the True One, unseen and infinite. Joining the two millstones (earth and sky), he set (them) apart; without the Guru there is pitch darkness. He created the sun and the moon (to light) the day and the night; reflect on (his) wondrous play. You are the True Master, true; you give true love. You created the earth; you are the giver of pain and pleasure. Creating woman and man, (you created) the poison of Maya, attachment and love. The sources of life and the tongues are yours; you give support to (all) beings. You have made creation your throne; you settle (all) in truth. You created coming and going; you, the Maker, are eternal. Bound in vices, the soul is born and dies, comes and goes. The wretched one has forgotten the Name; once drowned, what remedy is there for him? Leaving virtues, he has loaded poison, a trader in faults. The summons have come for those dear ones, by the Hukam of the True Creator. Wife and husband are parted; (he alone) unites the parted. (Jam) does not regard the beauty of the lovely woman; by the Hukam the task is laid on his head. (Jam's messengers) do not consider child or old; they break bonds of love and affection. By the Hukam of the True One the nine doors are shut, and the swan has flown to the sky. The wife is left alone, robbed by falsehood, widowed; the corpse lies in the courtyard at the door. O mother, at this death my senses have died, (she cries); the wife weeps at the door and the gate. O brides of the Husband, weep, cherishing the virtues of the True One. The dear one has been rubbed with water and bathed, and wrapped in clothes of silk. The true words are raised like music; the five (nearest kin) are as dead, stricken at heart. Parted from my dear one, it has been my death, (she cries); cursed is living in the world. That one alone is known (as true) who dies while yet alive, in love and affection for the True Husband. Weep, you who have come to weep: (you are) robbed by falsehood in the world. I am robbed, running after worldly business; the Husband has left me, (for my ways are those) of a woman without a lord. In every home the Husband (is with) the brides who are in love and affection for the Beautiful One. I must praise my true Husband; I am delighted in the Name of the Husband. Meeting the Guru, (her) guise is changed: the bride's adornment is the True One. Come, my friends, let us meet; remember the Creator. Through the Name the woman becomes a happy soul-bride; the True One is (her) adorner. Says Nanak: sing no song of separation; (sing) the contemplation of God. ॥8॥
The four sources of life (khaani): birth from the egg, from the womb, from sweat and from the earth. The tongues (bani): the speech of beings.
The nine doors: the nine openings of the body (two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, the mouth and the two lower openings).
The true words: the call Ram naam sat hai (the Lord's Name is true), raised as the bier is carried.
581.1: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). He who created the world and absorbs it (again): know that Master (to be in his) creation. Do not search for the True One far away; recognise the Shabad in every heart. Recognise the true Shabad; do not think him far away, who made this creation. When one meditates on the Naam, then one finds peace; without the Name the contest is lost. He who established (it) alone knows its way; what can anyone say to describe (it)? He who established the world and spread the net (over it): accept him as the Master. O brother, whoever has come must rise and go; the world is (but) a halt midway on the road. On every head the True One has written pain and pleasure, by the reckoning of (deeds done) before. He gives pain and pleasure as (each) has done; that goes along with the soul. (Each) does the deeds the Creator makes him do; he can seek no other work. He himself is detached; (the world) is bound in worldly business; issuing (his) Hukam, he sets (it) free. Saying today, tomorrow, one is seized by death; in the love of another, (all one does) is in vain. On the way of Jam the road cannot be seen; it is a wilderness, pitch dark. (There is) no water, no quilts or mattresses, no food of any kind. No food (given) with love, no cold water, no clothes or adornment. A chain is on his neck, (Jam) stands over his head and strikes (him); no house or home is to be seen. Seeds sown now do not sprout; he repents, with the load on his head. Without the True One no one is a friend; this is the true reflection. O brother, those who weep and repeat (the Name) are honoured, (as is one) who, joining (the Sangat), weeps, cherishing (God's) virtues. (She who is) robbed by Maya weeps; the weepers weep for worldly business. (Such a one) weeps for worldly business and does not wash off the filth; the world is (but) a dream. As at a juggler's show, (she) wanders in doubt and goes astray, robbed by falsehood, in pride. He himself sets (beings) on the path; he himself does the deeds. O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam the Perfect Guru has saved, (and they abide) in Sahaj and in love. ॥4॥
The -va at the end of lines here is a sung syllable of the dirge's measure; it is not rendered.
581.2: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O brother, whoever has come must rise and go; this world is a false show. By serving the True One the true home (is found); (serving) the True One, (one becomes) pure and truthful. When in falsehood and greed one finds no acceptance (here), ahead too one gets no place. No one says (to him), come in, be seated; (he is) like a crow at a deserted house. Birth and death (bring) the great separation; the whole world perishes. Through greed, worldly business and Maya the world is led astray; Death stands (over it) and makes it weep. O brother, come, my brothers, let us embrace, and meeting together, let us give blessings. O brother, union with the True One never ends; let us give blessings for (union with) the Beloved. Give blessings, and practise devotion; for those (already) united, what (further) union (is there)? Some have strayed from the Name, from (their true) home and place; through the Guru's Shabad, (remembering) the True One is the (true) game. (Those) merged in the Shabad do not go by the way of Jam; age after age (they abide) in the True One's form. O friends and kin, meet with those who join (others to the Lord), who, meeting the Guru, have untied (their) nooses. O brother, (one) comes naked into the world, with pain and pleasure written as (his) lot. The written hour (of departure), fixed by what (one) earned before, is not put off. The True One sat and wrote Amrit or poison; to whatever he attached (him), to that he is attached. The enchantress (Maya) has cast her spells, (and put) a many-coloured thread round (his) neck. With shallow understanding the mind has become shallow; he has eaten (Maya's bait) as the fly eats molasses. Naked he came into the world, and naked he is bound and driven off. O brother, weep if anyone must weep: the dear one has been bound and sent off. No one can erase the written lot; from (the Lord's) door the summons has come. The summons came when it pleased him, and the mourners wept. Sons, brothers, nephews and the dearest loved ones weep. (Let one) weep in (God's) fear, cherishing and recalling (his) virtues; no one dies with the dead. O Nanak, in every age they are known as wise who weep, keeping the True One in mind. ॥4॥
Saha: the day fixed for a wedding, when the bride leaves her parents' home and which cannot be put off; here the appointed hour of leaving the world.
582.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Let us praise God, the True Lord; he is able to do every task, all there is. That soul-bride never sits as a widow, nor does she ever grieve. She never grieves; night and day she enjoys delights, that soul-bride, absorbed in (her Husband's) mansion: she who has known the Beloved, who shapes (each) by their deeds, and who speaks the Amrit word. The virtuous ones dwell on (his) virtues and keep their Husband cherished (in the heart); separation never befalls them. Let us praise the True Husband, who is able to do all there is. The True Master is recognised through the Shabad; he himself unites (one with himself). That soul-bride is dyed in the Beloved's love who sheds self-conceit from within. She who sheds self-conceit from within is consumed by death no more; through the Guru she has known the One alone.
