The bride's longing has been fulfilled, she is drenched (with love) within; the Giver, the Life of the world, has met her. Dyed in the love of the Shabad, intoxicated with youth, she rests merged in her Husband's embrace. The True Master is recognised through the Shabad; he himself unites (one with himself). I go and ask those Sants who have recognised their own Husband. Leaving self-conceit, I serve (them); the True Husband is met in Sahaj and in love. The True Husband comes and meets her who practises Truth; the soul-bride stays dyed in the True Shabad. She is never a widow, ever a happy soul-bride; within her is the Samadhi of Sahaj. The Husband pervades everywhere, to the full; see him close at hand, and rejoice in him in Sahaj and in love. I go and ask those Sants who have recognised their own Husband. Even we, parted from the Husband, may meet (him), if we cling to the feet of the True Guru, the True One. The True Guru is ever merciful; he burns away faults through the Shabad. Burning away faults through the Shabad, he takes away the love of another, and (the soul-bride) is dyed in the True One alone. Through the True Shabad she has found lasting peace, and (her) Haumai and wandering have gone. The Husband is pure, ever the giver of peace; O Nanak, (the Guru) unites (one with him) through the Shabad. Even we, parted from the Husband, may meet (him), if we cling to the feet of the True Guru, the True One. ॥4॥
583.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Listen, O brides of the Husband: serve the Husband, reflecting through the Shabad. The one full of faults does not know the Husband; forgetting the Husband, she weeps, robbed. (She who) weeps holding the Husband dear, ever dwelling on (his) virtues: (her) Husband neither dies nor goes away. Through the Guru she has known (him), through the Shabad recognised (him), and she merges in true love. She who has not known her Husband, who shapes (each) by their deeds, the false one, is robbed by falsehood. Listen, O brides of the Husband: serve the Husband, reflecting through the Shabad. He himself has created all the world; the world is a coming and going. Through attachment to Maya he has led (it) astray; (the soul-bride) dies and is born again and again. Dying and being born again and again, her vices grow; devoid of wisdom, she is robbed. Without the Shabad she did not find the Husband, and has wasted her life; full of faults, the false one weeps. The Husband is the Life of the world: for whom should one weep? She who forgets the Husband weeps. He himself has created all the world; the world is a coming and going. That Husband is true, ever true; he neither dies nor goes away. The ignorant soul-bride wanders astray; in the love of another, she sits as a widow. In the love of another she sits as a widow; in attachment to Maya she suffers pain, her span of life shrinks, her body wastes away. Whatever has come will all go; through the love of another, pain has taken hold. Jamkaal is not seen; the world quarrels over Maya, and sets its mind on greed and avarice. That Husband is true, ever true; he neither dies nor goes away. Some, parted from the Husband, weep; the blind one does not know that the Husband is with (her). By the Guru's grace the True Husband is met (by her who) ever cherishes (him) within. (For her who) cherishes the Husband within, he is ever with (her); the manmukh has thought (him) far away. This body of the one who did not know the Master close at hand is knocked about and wasted, of no use. O Nanak, that soul-bride, united (by the Guru), meets (him), who keeps the Husband ever cherished within. Some, parted from the Husband, weep; the blind one does not know that the Husband is with (her). ॥4॥
584.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those parted from the Husband weep; my Husband is true, and is ever with (me). Those who have known for certain that they must depart serve the True Guru, cherishing the Naam. (For one who) ever cherishes the Naam, the True Guru is with (him); serving the True Guru, (he) has found peace. Slaying death through the Shabad and enshrining the True One in the heart, (he) has no more coming and going. True is the Master, true his glory; he watches over (all), looking on with his glance of grace. Those parted from the Husband weep; my Husband is true, and is ever with (me). My God, the Master, is higher than all: how am I to meet the dear Beloved? When the True Guru joined (me to him), I met (him) in Sahaj, and kept the Husband enshrined in (my) heart. Keeping him ever enshrined in the heart, (I hold) love for the Beloved; through the True Guru the Husband is seen. The robe of attachment to Maya is of a fleeting dye; wearing it, the foot slips. The robe dyed in the Husband's love is true (and fast); wearing it, (one) puts thirst away. My God, the Master, is higher than all: how am I to meet the dear Beloved? I have recognised God, the True One; any other, full of faults, has gone astray. My own Husband ever delights in me, as I reflect through the True Shabad. Reflecting through the True Shabad, the bride is dyed in (his) love; meeting the True Guru, she has found the Beloved. Within, she is dyed in love, intoxicated in Sahaj; every enemy and every pain has gone. Let body and mind be given to one's own Guru; then the mind is drenched (with love), and (the Guru) dispels the pains of craving. I have recognised the Husband, the True One; any other, full of faults, has gone astray. The True One created the world himself; without the Guru, all is pitch dark. He himself unites, he himself meets, he himself gives love. He himself gives love, and the trade (in the Name) in Sahaj; through the Guru he makes (one's) life beautiful. Blessed is the coming into the world of one who has shed self-conceit; at the door of the True One, (he) is found true. Through the jewel of wisdom, light has dawned in (his) heart; O Nanak, the Naam is dear (to him). The True One created the world himself; without the Guru, all is pitch dark. ॥4॥
584.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). This body is frail and wearing out; old age comes and overtakes it. Those whom the Guru has protected are saved; any other dies and is born, comes and goes. The others die and are born, come and go, and departing at the end, they regret; without the Name there is no peace. What one earns here, that fruit one receives; the manmukh has lost (his) honour. In the city of Jam is pitch darkness, deep gloom; there is neither sister nor brother there. This body is frail and wearing out; old age comes and overtakes it. Only then does the body become gold, when the True Guru unites (one with the Lord). (Then) the delusion of Maya is cut away from within, and (one) merges in the True Name. Merged in the True Name, he sings the Lord's praises, and meeting the Beloved, finds peace. He stays ever in bliss, day and night, and Haumai leaves (him) from within. Those who have fixed their mind on the Lord's Name: I fall at their feet. Only then does the body become gold, when the True Guru unites (one with the Lord). That True One, the ever-True, is praised (only) if the True Guru grants understanding. Without the True Guru, (the soul-brides) are led astray by doubt; what face will they show in the world beyond, once they have gone? Having gone (there), what face can they show? (Each) regrets her faults, and earns pain upon pain. Those who are imbued with the Name are dyed deep red, and rest merged in the Husband's embrace. None as great as he is to be seen; before whom (else) should one go and speak? That True One, the ever-True, is praised (only) if the True Guru grants understanding. Those who have praised the True One, the ever-True: I fall at their feet. Those people are true and spotless; meeting them, all filth goes. Meeting them, all filth goes; (one) bathes in the true pool, and (abides) in the True One, in Sahaj and in love. The True Guru has given understanding of the Name, immaculate, beyond reach and beyond the senses. Night and day they perform devotion, dyed in (his) love; O Nanak, they stay merged in the True One. Those who have meditated on the True One, the ever-True: I fall at their feet. ॥4॥
585.1: Vadhans ki Vaar: by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji); to be sung to the tune of Lalan Behlima. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those dyed in the Shabad, with the True Name enshrined in their hearts, are the great swans; they gather Truth, and abide ever in the True One, in love with the True Name. They are ever spotless, no filth clings (to them); the Creator has cast his glance of grace (on them). I, Nanak, am a sacrifice to those who repeat (the Name of) Murari night and day. ॥1॥

The pauris of Vadhans ki Vaar are the Fourth Guru's; each is preceded by saloks, most of them the Third Guru's. Lalan Behlima: by tradition Lalan and Behlima, two Rajput chiefs of the Kangra country; in a drought Lalan took water from Behlima's canal, promising a sixth of his crop, and broke his word; the bards sang their fight as a vaar, and this vaar is to be sung to its tune (dhuni). Vadh hans (great swan) in the first salok is the raag's own name.
585.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). I took him for a great swan, and so I kept his company; had I known him to be a wretched heron, I would never have come near him at all. ॥2॥
585.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Seeing the swans swimming, the herons too grew eager; (but) the wretched herons drowned and died, heads down and feet up. ॥3॥
585.4: (O Lord,) you yourself, you alone, are all there is; you yourself made the root (of creation). You yourself are the Formless One; there is no other, no second. You are the Cause of creation, all-powerful; whatever you do comes about. You give gifts unasked to all beings. Say, all of you: praise, praise to the True Guru, who has put the gift of the Lord's Name into (our) mouths. ॥1॥
586.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). All that has form is in fear; the dear Lord alone is without fear. When the True Guru is served, the Lord dwells in the mind; there, fear never comes. No enemy, no pain comes near him; none can touch him. The Gurmukh has reflected in the mind: whatever pleases him (the Lord) comes to pass. O Nanak, he himself will preserve (one's) honour; it is he who sets (one's) affairs right. ॥1॥
586.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Some friends are leaving, some have left; those who remain will go in their turn too. Those who have not served the True Guru come and go, and regret. O Nanak, those imbued with the True One are not parted (from him); serving the True Guru, they merge (in him). ॥2॥
586.3: Let us meet that friend, the True Guru, within whom is the Lord, the giver of virtues. Let us meet that beloved True Guru, who has slain Haumai from within. Blessed, blessed is that perfect True Guru, who, by giving the Lord's teaching, has set right the whole world. Repeat ever, O Sants, the Name of Ram, which carries (one) across the poisonous ocean of the world. The Perfect Guru has given (me) the Lord's teaching; to the Guru I am a sacrifice for ever. ॥2॥
586.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The service and work of the True Guru is the essence of the joy of all joys. Here (it) brings honours, and in the Lord's court, the door of liberation. True is the work (one) does, Truth (one's) clothing, the True Name (one's) support. Through the true company (one) meets the True One, and there is love for the True Name. Through the True Shabad there is ever joy; at the True door (one) is found true. O Nanak, the service of the True Guru is done by him alone on whom the Creator casts his glance of grace. ॥1॥
586.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In other service, service to another (than the Lord), life is cursed, and cursed the dwelling. Leaving the Amrit, they cling to poison; poison is their earning, poison their capital. Poison is their food, poison their wear, mouthfuls of poison in their mouths. Here they earn pain upon pain, and when they die, their dwelling is in hell. The manmukhs, with soiled faces, do not know the Shabad; they are ruined in lust and anger. They have cast off the fear of the True Guru; through the mind's stubbornness no work comes right. Bound in the city of Jam they are beaten; none hears their plea. O Nanak, one does what was written beforehand; the Gurmukhs dwell in the Name. ॥2॥
586.6: Serve that True Guru, the Saadh, who has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm (within). Worship day and night that True Guru who has had (us) repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world, the Master of the universe. Behold, every instant, that True Guru who has shown the way to the Lord, Har. Fall, all of you, at that True Guru's feet, who has ended the darkness of attachment. Call that True Guru blessed, blessed, all of you, who has brought (us) to the treasures of the Lord's devotion. ॥3॥
586.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Meeting the True Guru, hunger has gone; through (religious) garbs hunger does not go. Gripped by its pain, (the garb-wearer) goes about from door to door, and in the hereafter gets twice the punishment. Sahaj has not come within (him), so that he might take what comes and eat it in Sahaj. Whoever he begs from with a stubborn mind, he takes (from him) only by causing distress. Better than this garb is the householder, from whom someone gains (something). Those dyed in the Shabad have gained understanding; (others) go astray in the doubt of duality. One must act by the record (of past deeds) that has been laid down; nothing can be said (of it). O Nanak, those who please him are good, whose honour you, (O Lord,) accept. ॥1॥
587.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). By serving the True Guru there is peace for ever, and the pain of birth and death goes. No anxiety arises at all, (for) the Carefree (Lord) comes to dwell in the mind. Within (oneself) is the tirath of divine knowledge; the True Guru has made this known. The filth has gone and the mind has become pure, bathing at the tirath, the pool of Amrit. Friends have met friends, through the True Shabad, in love. In their own home they have found intimacy (with the Lord), merging (their) light in the Light. With hypocrisy, Jamkaal does not let (one) go; he will carry (the hypocrite) off, his honour lost. O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam are saved, fixing (their) attention on the True One. ॥2॥
587.2: Go and sit in that Sat Sangat where the Name of the Lord, Har, is churned. (There) take the Lord's Name in Sahaj, so that the essence, the Lord, is not lost. Repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, always, day and night, (and) shelter is found in the Lord's court. He alone finds the perfect True Guru on whose brow, on whose forehead, it is written from the very first. Let all bow before that Guru who has spoken the talk of the Lord, Har. ॥4॥
587.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Friends have met friends, those who love the True Guru. Meeting together, they have meditated on the Beloved; their love rests in true affection. From within itself the mind has come to believe, through the Guru's infinite Shabad. These friends, once met, do not part, whom the Creator himself has united. Some have not come to have faith in the sight (of the Guru); they do not reflect through the Shabad. What (more) separation can the separated suffer, whose affection is caught in the love of another? Friendship with a manmukh lasts but four short days. This love takes no time to break; from this friendship (only) vices flow. Those within whom there is no fear of the True One, who do not love the Naam: O Nanak, why make friends with them, whom the Creator himself has led astray? ॥1॥
587.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Some stay ever in the love of the One; to them I am for ever a sacrifice. I would offer them body, mind and wealth, and bow down again and again at their feet. Meeting them, the mind is contented, and all craving and hunger go. O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam are ever at peace, fixing (their) attention on the True One. ॥2॥
587.5: I am a sacrifice to that Guru who has told (me) the story of the Lord, Har. To that Guru I am for ever a sacrifice, who has laid down the way of the Lord's service. That beloved True Guru is with me; he sets me free wherever (I am). Praise be to that Guru, who has given (me) understanding of the Lord. Nanak is a sacrifice to the Guru, who has given the Lord's Name and fulfilled my mind's hope. ॥5॥
588.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Scorched by craving, (the world) has burned to death; burning and burning, it cries out. If it meets the cooling True Guru, it will not burn again a second time. O Nanak, without the Name no one is free of fear, so long as one does not reflect through the Shabad. ॥1॥
588.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through (religious) garbs the fire (of craving) is not quenched; anxiety remains in the mind. Beat the snake's hole and the snake does not die: just so are the deeds of those without a Guru. If the True Guru, the Giver, is served, the Shabad comes to dwell in the mind. Mind and body become cool and at peace, and the fire of craving is put out. There is lasting peace, the crown of all comforts, when one rids oneself of self-conceit from within. Through the Guru, he alone practises (true) detachment who keeps (his) attention fixed on the True One. No anxiety arises (in him) at all; he is fully sated with the Lord's Name. O Nanak, without the Name there is no release; (people) burn and are consumed in Haumai. ॥2॥
588.3: Those who have meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have obtained every comfort. Fruitful is the whole life of those in whose minds hunger for the Lord's Name has arisen. Those who have worshipped (the Lord) through the Guru's word have forgotten all (their) sorrows. Those Sants, the Gursikhs, are good, who do not look in the least to another (besides the Lord). Blessed, blessed is their Guru, whose mouth bears the Lord's Amrit fruit. ॥6॥
588.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Kalyug Jam is merciless, (yet) he does (his) work only by (God's) Hukam. Those whom the Guru has protected are saved; on the manmukhs he inflicts punishment. The world is held bound in the power of Jamkaal, and it has no one to protect it. Serve the One who made Jam; through the Guru, (then) no pain comes. O Nanak, Jam serves the Gurmukhs, in whose minds the True One is. ॥1॥
Kalyug: in the reckoning of the Puranas, the fourth and darkest of the world's four ages, held to be the present one.
588.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). This body is full of disease; without the Shabad the pain, the disease of Haumai, does not go. If the True Guru is met, then one becomes pure and enshrines the Lord's Name alone in the mind. O Nanak, (those who) have meditated on the Name of the Giver of peace have forgotten (their) pain, in Sahaj and in love. ॥2॥
588.6: The Guru who has taught (me of) the Life of the world: to that Guru I am ever a sacrifice. To that Guru I am cut in pieces as a sacrifice, who has made (me) hear the Name of the Lord, Madhusudan. To that Guru I am offered up, who has rid (me) of the poison of Haumai, the whole disease. Great is the good done by that True Guru who, cutting away (my) failings, has made (me) understand the Lord of virtues. That True Guru has met those on whose face and brow (good) fortune was written and set. ॥7॥
589.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The marjeevre, dead (to self) while alive, perform devotion; through the Guru, devotion goes on for ever. On them (the Lord) has bestowed from the very first the treasure of devotion; no one can erase it. Within the mind they have found the Treasure of virtues, the one True Lord. O Nanak, through the Guru they remain united (with him), and never again is there separation. ॥1॥
Marjeevra is also the word for the pearl-diver, who plunges into the sea and comes up with pearls.
589.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (The one who) has not served the True Guru: what reflection can he make? He does not know the worth of the Shabad; the fool is lost in the poison (of Maya). The blind, ignorant one performs many (ritual) deeds, (but his) affection is caught in the love of another. Being nothing, they count themselves (great); Jam strikes them and brings them to ruin. O Nanak, to whom is one to speak, when (the Lord) himself is the Forgiver? ॥2॥
589.3: You are the Creator, you know everything; all beings are yours. Whomever you will, you join to yourself; what (power) have the poor creatures? You are the all-powerful Cause of creation, O True Creator. The one whom you unite (with yourself), O Beloved, meets you, reflecting (on you) through the Guru. I am a sacrifice to my own True Guru, by whom my Lord, the Unknowable, has been made known (to me). ॥8॥
589.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One who is an assayer of jewels reflects on jewels. The ignorant one, blind and in darkness, does not know the worth of jewels. The jewel is the Guru's Shabad; one who has understanding understands (this). Fools count themselves (great); they die and are born (again), and are ruined. O Nanak, the jewels are found by the one in whom love wells up through the Guru. He utters the Naam for ever and ever; the Lord's Name alone is his daily dealing. If (the Lord) shows his own grace, then I may keep the Lord enshrined in my heart. ॥1॥
589.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who have not served the True Guru, nor come to love the Lord's Name: do not think they are alive; the Creator himself has struck them dead. Haumai is a great disease; (in it) one acts in the love of another. O Nanak, the manmukhs are dead while alive; forgetting the Lord, they suffer pain. ॥2॥
589.6: One whose inner heart is pure: before that person all bow. One within whom is the treasure of the Naam: to that person I am a sacrifice. One within whom is a discerning intellect, (and) the Name of the Lord, Murari: that True Guru is the friend of all; all are dear to him. The Lord who pervades every soul has spread out all (this): so the Guru's understanding has seen. ॥9॥
589.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Without serving the True Guru, the deeds (people) do in Haumai are bonds for the soul. Without serving the True Guru, they find no resting place; they die and are born, and come and go. Without serving the True Guru, (their) speech is insipid, and the Naam does not dwell in the mind. O Nanak, without serving the True Guru, (such people) are tied up and beaten in Jam's city, and go from here with blackened faces. ॥1॥
590.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Let me burn such a way (of life) through which I forget the Beloved. O Nanak, that love alone is good through which one's honour is kept with the Master. ॥2॥
590.2: Serve the Lord, the one Giver; meditate on the one Lord. Ask of the Lord, the one Giver, (and) what the mind longs for is obtained. If one asks of another, one dies of shame. Whoever has served (him) has obtained the fruit; all the hunger of that servant is taken away. Nanak is a sacrifice to those who meditate night and day on the Lord's Name in their hearts. ॥10॥
590.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). My Beloved is himself pleased with (his) devotees; he himself has attached (his) servants (to himself). To the devotees he has given kingship; the Lord has fashioned the true royal canopy over their heads. Doing the True Guru's work, they are ever at peace and pure. Those are not to be called kings who fight and die, and then fall into (the round of) births. O Nanak, without the Name they go about with their noses cut off (in disgrace), and win no honour at all. ॥1॥
590.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Hearing the teaching (alone), no relish has come, so long as one is not joined, through the Guru, to the Shabad. By serving the True Guru the Naam dwells in the mind, and doubt and fear flee from within. When one becomes such as one knows the True Guru to be, then (one's) attention is fixed on the True Name. O Nanak, through the Name greatness is received, and (such ones) shine at the Lord's door hereafter. ॥2॥
590.5: In the minds of the Gursikhs is love for the Lord; they come to worship the Guru. With love they trade in the Lord's Name, and carry away the Lord's Name as (their) profit. The faces of the Gursikhs are radiant; they are pleasing in the Lord's court. The Guru, the True Guru, is the heap (of threshed grain) of the Lord's Name; the fortunate Sikhs enter into partnership (with him) in virtues. I am a sacrifice to those Gursikhs who keep meditating on the Lord's Name as they sit and as they rise. ॥11॥
590.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O Nanak, the Naam is the treasure; it is found through the Guru. The manmukhs do not know the thing that lies in their own house; the blind ones die barking and wailing. ॥1॥
590.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Golden and spotless is the body that, through the True Name, is joined to the True One. It has found the Immaculate One, the spotless Light; through the Guru, its doubt and fear have fled. O Nanak, the Gurmukhs, night and day detached (from the world) in longing for the Lord, ever find peace. ॥2॥
590.8: Blessed, blessed are those Gursikhs who have heard with their own ears the Guru's teaching of the Lord. The one in whom the Guru, the True Guru, has made the Naam firm has shattered Haumai and duality. Apart from the Lord's Name there is no friend: the Lord's servants have reflected and seen it so. The Gursikhs with whom the Lord is pleased have accepted the True Guru's word. Those who meditate on the Naam through the Guru are dyed in a fourfold colour (of love). ॥12॥
591.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The manmukh is a coward and ill-favoured; without the Name he has no nose (no honour). Day and night he is caught up in worldly affairs; not even in a dream does he have peace. O Nanak, if (manmukhs) become Gurmukh, they are saved; otherwise they suffer pain, held in bonds. ॥1॥
591.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The Gurmukhs look ever beautiful at (the Lord's) door; they live by the Guru's Shabad. Within them is calm and ever peace; at the true door they receive honour. O Nanak, the Gurmukhs have obtained the Lord's Name; in Sahaj they stay merged in the True One. ॥2॥
591.3: Through the Guru, Prahlad meditated on the Lord and attained liberation. Through the Guru, Janak fixed his attention on the Lord's Name. Through the Guru, Basisht imparted the Lord's teaching. No one has found the Lord's Name without the Guru, O my brother. Through the Guru, the Lord himself has granted devotion to himself. ॥13॥

Prahlad, son of the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu), held to devotion to God through all his father's torments. Janak, king of Mithila and father of Sita, is remembered as a sage who stayed detached while he ruled. Basisht (Vasishtha) was the sage who was guru to Ram's house; his teaching to Ram is told in the Yoga Vasishtha.
591.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One who has not come to trust the True Guru, and whose love has not taken to the Shabad, finds no peace welling up within, though he come and go (to the Guru) a hundred times. O Nanak, through the Guru (the Lord) is met in Sahaj, if one fixes one's attention on the True One. ॥1॥
591.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O mind, search out and find such a True Guru, serving whom the pain of birth and death goes away, no anxiety arises at all, and Haumai is burnt away through the Shabad, the wall of falsehood is taken out from within, and the True One comes to dwell in the mind, and there is calm within and peace in the mind, as one does one's work in the discipline of truth. O Nanak, the True Guru is met through perfect grace, when the dear Lord shows mercy by his own will. ॥2॥
591.6: The one in whose house the Lord is the Diwan (the ruler): the whole world has come into his fist. He is beholden to no one; the Lord, the Diwan, has brought all and set them at his feet. From a court of men someone may run and get away, (but) from the Lord's court where could anyone go? Such a Diwan, the Lord, dwells in the hearts of the devotees; he has brought all the rest, every last one, and made them stand before the devotees. The glory of the Lord's Name is obtained by (his) grace; some rare one, through the Guru, has meditated (on it). ॥14॥
591.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Without serving the True Guru the world has died, wasting its life in vain. In the love of another, great pain has struck it; it dies and is born, and comes and goes. Its dwelling is in filth, and it falls into births again and again. O Nanak, without the Name Jam will strike it down, and at the end it departs repenting. ॥1॥
591.8: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In this world there is one Purakh, the Husband; all the rest, the whole creation, is (his) bride. He enjoys every body, yet stays untouched; he is the Unseen, and cannot be seen. The perfect Guru has shown (him), and through the Shabad has given understanding (of him). Those who serve the Purakh become purakhs (like him): those who have burnt Haumai through the Shabad. He has no rival, nor any enemy to pierce him like a thorn. His rule is unshakable for ever; he neither comes nor goes. Night and day (his) servant serves (him) and sings the virtues of the True Lord. Nanak has blossomed, beholding the glory of the True Lord. ॥2॥
592.1: Those in whose hearts the Lord's Name ever dwells: the Lord's Name alone is their protector. The Lord's Name is (our) father, the Lord's Name alone (our) mother; the Lord's Name is our helper and friend. With the Lord's Name is (our) talk, with the Lord's Name (our) counsel; the Lord's Name takes care of us every day. The Lord's Name is our company, most dear; the Lord's Name is (our) lineage, the Lord's Name (our) family. To servant Nanak the Guru has given the Lord's Name; the Lord ever brings (him) across, in this world and the next. ॥15॥
592.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who have met the True Guru ever practise the Lord's praise. The Name of the carefree Lord has come to dwell in their minds, and they stay merged in the True Shabad. They save their whole lineage, and themselves attain the state of liberation. The Supreme Lord is well pleased with the people who fall at the feet of the Guru. Servant Nanak is a slave of the Lord; in his mercy the Lord keeps (his) honour. ॥1॥
592.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In Haumai there is dread within, and (life) passes in dread upon dread. Haumai is a great disease; (in it one) dies and is born, comes and goes. Those for whom it was so written from the first have met the True Guru, and God has come (to meet them). O Nanak, by the Guru's grace they are saved, burning away Haumai through the Shabad. ॥2॥
592.4: The Lord's Name is our God: unmanifest, beyond the senses, imperishable, the all-pervading Being, the Maker. We serve the Lord's Name, we worship the Lord's Name; (our) mind is dyed in the Lord's Name alone. None other as great as the Lord's Name comes to mind; the Lord's Name alone sets free at the end. The Guru, the benefactor of others, has given the Lord's Name; blessed, blessed are the father and mother of the Guru. I ever bow to my True Guru, meeting whom I have come to know the Lord's Name. ॥16॥
592.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One who has not served through the Guru, whose love has not taken to the Lord's Name, (and) who has not tasted the savour of the Shabad, dies and is born again and again. The blind manmukh does not remember (the Lord): for what has he come into the world? O Nanak, those on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace cross over through the Guru. ॥1॥
592.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The True Guru alone is awake; the rest of the world sleeps in attachment and thirst. Those who serve the True Guru stay awake: those dyed in the True Name of the treasure of virtues. The blind manmukhs do not remember (the Lord); being born and dying, they are ruined. O Nanak, they alone have meditated on the Naam through the Guru for whom it was so written at the Source, from the first. ॥2॥
593.1: The Lord's Name is our food of thirty-six kinds, eating which we are fully satisfied. The Lord's Name is our clothing, wearing which we shall never again be naked, and our wish to wear anything else is gone. The Lord's Name is our trade, the Lord's Name our business; the True Guru has made us stewards of the Lord's Name. We have written up the account of the Lord's Name alone, and all our old subjection to Jam is gone. Some rare one, through the Guru, has meditated on the Lord's Name: those for whom, by (his) grace, the writ of receiving it was set down at the Source. ॥17॥
593.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The world is ignorant and blind; it does its deeds in the love of another. Whatever deeds it does in the love of another, pain comes rushing to strike its body. By the Guru's grace peace wells up, when one lives by the Guru's Shabad, does one's deeds through the True Bani, and meditates on the Naam night and day. O Nanak, to whatever (the Lord) himself attaches (beings), to that they are attached; nothing can be said (of it). ॥1॥
593.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In our house is the treasure of the Naam for ever, (and) the storehouses brim with devotion. The True Guru is the giver of life to the soul; the Giver lives for ever. Night and day, through the Guru's Shabad, we ever sing the Kirtan of the Infinite (Lord). We ever utter the Guru's Shabad, which deals out (the gift of the Name) age after age. This mind (of ours) dwells ever in peace, and carries on (its) trade (in the Name) in Sahaj. Within is the Guru's wisdom, the jewel of the Lord, which brings liberation. O Nanak, the one on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace obtains (it), and is found true at (his) door. ॥2॥
593.4: Blessed, blessed must that Gursikh be called who has gone and fallen at the True Guru's feet. Blessed, blessed must that Gursikh be called who has uttered with his mouth the Lord's Name, Ram. Blessed, blessed must that Gursikh be called whose mind has filled with bliss on hearing the Lord's Name. Blessed, blessed must that Gursikh be called who, by serving the True Guru, has received the Lord's Name. I ever bow to that Gursikh, the Gursikh who walks in the Guru's will. ॥18॥
593.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). By the stubbornness of the mind no one has found (him); all have grown weary of performing rites. By the mind's stubbornness (people) put on (holy) garbs and wander, and in the love of another they have met with pain. Riddhis and siddhis (wealth and miraculous powers) are all attachment; (through them) the Naam does not come to dwell in the mind. Through service to the Guru the mind becomes pure, and the darkness of ignorance goes. (When) the jewel of the Naam is revealed in the house (within), O Nanak, (one) merges in Sahaj. ॥1॥
593.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). One who has not tasted the savour of the Shabad, whose love has not taken to the Name, speaks insipid words with his tongue, and is ruined day after day. O Nanak, one must act by the record (of past deeds) that has been laid down; no one can erase it. ॥2॥
594.1: Blessed, blessed is our True Guru, the True Being, meeting whom calm has come to us. Blessed, blessed is our True Guru, the True Being, meeting whom we have obtained devotion to the Lord. Blessed, blessed is our True Guru, the Lord's devotee, by serving whom we have fixed our attention on the Lord's Name. Blessed, blessed is our True Guru, who knows the Lord, who has shown us how to see all, enemy and friend, with an equal eye. Blessed, blessed is the True Guru, our friend, who has formed our love for the Lord's Name. ॥19॥
594.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The Husband is right at home, (yet) the bride (thinks him) gone abroad; every day she pines and remembers (him). There is no delay in meeting (him), if she makes her intention right. ॥1॥
594.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, false is the talk one makes without love; one holds (the Lord) good only so long as he gives and one receives. ॥2॥
594.4: The Lord who created the beings has himself protected (them). (They) have tasted the Amrit, the True Name, as their food. They are satisfied and fully sated, (and their) hunger is stilled. The One pervades within all, (but) some rare one has perceived (him). O servant Nanak, (they) have been made joyful, with God on their side. ॥20॥
594.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Everyone looks upon the True Guru, the whole world, all there is of it; (but) seeing (him) brings no liberation, so long as one does not reflect on the Shabad. (Till then) the filth of Haumai does not go, and love for the Name does not take hold. Some (the Lord) himself has forgiven and united (with himself); they have cast off duality and the vices. O Nanak, some, beholding the sight (of the Guru), have died (to the self) and been united, in love and affection for the True Guru. ॥1॥
594.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The fool, blind and ignorant, has not served the True Guru; in the love of another, great pain has struck him, and he cries out as he burns. Those for whose sake he forgot the Guru are of no help (to him) at the final hour. O Nanak, through the Guru's teaching (one) has found peace; the Forgiver forgives (that one). ॥2॥
594.7: (O God,) you are all by yourself, and you yourself are the Maker of everything; were there any second, only then could we call him another. The Lord himself speaks and himself makes (all) speak; the Lord himself pervades the water and the land. The Lord himself kills and the Lord himself spares; O mind, let us stay fallen at the Lord's refuge. Without the Lord no one can kill or give life; (so), O mind, let us rest free of care, at ease, with limbs stretched out. Rising, sitting and sleeping, ever and always, let us meditate on the Lord's Name; O servant Nanak, through the Guru the Lord is found.
Nisal: lying at ease, the body loosened and the limbs stretched out; that is, hoping in no one else and fearing no one else.
Sudh (corrected): written after the closing numbers of the vaar, it marks that the text was checked against the original.

557.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Vadhans, Ghar 1, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If the addict does not get his drug, if the fish has no water, (nothing pleases them);
(but) to those imbued with their own Husband (Lord), everyone is dear.
I am a sacrifice, cut in pieces as a sacrifice, to your Name, O Master.
The Master is a tree laden with fruit, whose Name is Amrit (the nectar of immortal life);
those who have drunk (it) are fulfilled; I am a sacrifice to them.
(O Lord,) you do not come into my sight, though you dwell with all.
How is the thirsty one's thirst to go, when a wall stands between (him and) the pool?
Nanak is your trader; you are the Master, (and you are) my capital.
Anxiety leaves the mind only when I sing (your) praise and pray (to you). ॥4॥
557.2: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The virtuous (soul-bride) has enjoyed her Husband's love; why does the one without virtue cry out?
If she becomes virtuous, then she too can go to enjoy her Husband's love.
My Husband is the source of delight, dear friend; why should the bride enjoy others?
If (good) deeds become the love-charm, if the mind becomes the thread,
(then) the ruby, not to be had for any price, is won by threading it into the consciousness.
I ask the way but do not walk it, and (yet) I say I have arrived.
With you, my Husband, I am not even on speaking terms; how can I come to dwell in (your) house?
O Nanak, apart from the One there is no other.
If (a bride) stays attached to you, my Husband, then she enjoys her Husband's love. ॥4॥
557.3: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 2, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The peacocks have struck up their sweet calls, O sister; Saavan (the month of the rains) has come.
(O Lord,) these (sights) of yours are a dagger and a noose for the bride; this (beauty of yours) has drawn me, who long (for you), with longing.
I am cut in pieces as a sacrifice to the sight of you; I am a sacrifice to your Name.
Because you are (mine), I have taken pride; without you, what pride have I?
Break your bangles against the bed, O young bride, together with (its) side-frames and (your) arms;
O young bride, adorning yourself in so many ways, (your) Husband is in love with others.
Neither the bangle-seller, nor the bangles, nor those glass bangles (are of any use);
may the arms that have not embraced the Husband's neck burn.
All (my) friends have gone to enjoy the Husband's love; to whose door shall I, the burnt one, go?
O friend, I (count myself) most well-mannered, (yet) I do not please you, my Husband, by even one (virtue).
I have my plaits braided with care, and the parting of my hair is filled with vermilion;
(yet) going before (him), I am not accepted; I die, grieving and grieving.
As I weep, the whole world has wept; the birds of the forest have wept too;
only one has not wept: the separation within my body, which has parted me from my Beloved.
He came in a dream and went again; I wept, (my eyes) brimming with tears.
I cannot come to you, Beloved, nor can I send anyone.
Come, blessed sleep; perhaps I may see that Husband (again).
The one who tells (me) a word of you, my Master, says Nanak, what should (I) give him?
One should cut off one's head and give it (him) for a seat, and serve (him) without a head.
Why should one not die, why not give up one's life, when the Husband has become a stranger? ॥1॥
558.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 1, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
When the mind is soiled, all is soiled; washing the body does not make the mind clean.
This world is led astray by doubt; rare is the one who understands (this).
O my mind, repeat the one Name;
this is the treasure the True Guru has given me.
If one learns the postures of the Siddhas (yogis held to be perfected), and practises (them), holding the senses in check,
(still) the filth of the mind does not come off, the filth of Haumai (ego) does not go.
For this mind there is no other discipline but the refuge of the True Guru.
Meeting the True Guru, (the mind's attention) is turned back (from the world); nothing can be said (of it).
Says Nanak: whoever, meeting the True Guru, dies (to the self) and through the Guru's Shabad lives again,
the filth of the sense of mine comes off (him), and this mind becomes clean. ॥4॥
558.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through (God's) glance of grace the True Guru is served; through his glance of grace service is done;
through his glance of grace this mind comes under control; through his glance of grace the mind becomes pure.
O my mind, remember that True One.
If you remember the One, you will find peace, and then there will be no sorrow at all.
Through his glance of grace one dies (to the self) and lives; through his glance of grace the Shabad comes to dwell in the mind.
Through his glance of grace the Hukam (God's will) is understood, and (one) stays merged in the Hukam.
The tongue that has not tasted the Lord's essence, may that tongue burn;
it stayed attached to the tastes of other pleasures, and in the love of another it found pain.
The glance of the One is on all; he himself makes the difference (between them).
O Nanak, meeting the True Guru, (one) has found the fruit; (God) grants the Naam and honour. ॥4॥
559.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Attachment to Maya (the world's illusion and lure) is pitch darkness; without the Guru there is no (spiritual) wisdom.
Those attached to the Shabad have understood; in the love of another the world's people are ruined.
O my mind, keep to the way of life of the Guru's teaching.
If you dwell on the Lord God for ever and ever, you will find the door of liberation.
The One is the treasure of virtues; only when he himself gives does anyone receive (it).
Without the Name all are parted (from him); through the Guru's Shabad he unites (them).
Crying mine, mine, they wasted away; nothing came into their hands.
Meeting the True Guru, (they) met the True One and merged in the True Name.
This body is (caught in) hope and desire; (God) lights the Light within (it).
O Nanak, the manmukh (the self-willed) is in bondage; through the Guru (God) brings liberation. ॥4॥
559.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The faces of the happy soul-brides are ever radiant; through the Guru (they abide) in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and in love.
Shedding the self from within, they ever enjoy their Husband's love.
Meditate, O my mind, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
for the True Guru has made the Lord known to me.
The forsaken soul-brides wail bitterly; they do not find (the Husband's) mansion.
Made ugly by the love of another, they suffer pain when they go on (to the world) beyond.
The virtuous (soul-bride), enshrining the Naam in her heart, dwells on (his) virtues every day;
the wife full of faults is struck by pain and wails.
The one Master is the Husband of all; nothing can be said (of him).
O Nanak, he himself has made (them) distinct, (and some) he has attached to the Name. ॥4॥
559.3: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Amrit Name has become ever sweet (to me), for through the Guru's Shabad its savour has come;
through the true Bani (my attention) is merged in Sahaj, and (I) have enshrined the dear Lord in my mind.
The Lord, in his mercy, has brought (me) to the True Guru;
through the perfect True Guru (I) have meditated on the Lord's Name.
Brahma revealed the word of the Vedas, (but what spread from it was) attachment to Maya.
Mahadev (Shiva), the wise one, stays absorbed in his own house, (yet in him is) the darkness of tamas and much pride.
Kisan (Vishnu) is ever caught up in taking incarnations; holding to whom, (then), shall the world cross over?
Through the Guru, those steeped in (spiritual) wisdom in this age find the darkness of attachment ended.
Through service of the True Guru comes release; through the Guru the world crosses over.
The detached, imbued with the True Name, find the door of liberation.
The One True Lord pervades all, and cherishes all.
I, Nanak, know none but the One; the merciful One is the support of all. ॥5॥
559.4: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through the Guru (come) truth, self-discipline and the essence of wisdom;
through the Guru the attention is fixed on the True One.
O my mind, through the Guru, keep the Naam in your heart;
it stands by (you) always and goes along with you.
Through the Guru, that True One is (one's) caste and honour;
through the Guru, God becomes the companion within.
He alone becomes Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) whom (God) himself makes so;
through the Guru he himself gives glory.
Through the Guru, make the true Shabad your task and keep to it;
through the Guru, O Nanak, (one becomes) a support to (one's) family too. ॥4॥
560.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The tongue has taken to the Lord's taste, in Sahaj and in love;
meditating on the Lord's Name, the mind is satisfied.
There is lasting peace in reflecting on the True Shabad.
I am ever a sacrifice to my True Guru.
The eyes are content, fixing (their) attention on the One;
shedding the love of another, the mind is at rest.
Through the Shabad, through the Lord's Name, there is peace in the body;
the fragrance of the Naam pervades the heart.
O Nanak, the one on whose forehead is great good fortune
(gains), through the Guru's Bani, detachment in Sahaj. ॥4॥
560.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Naam is obtained from the perfect Guru;
through the True Shabad (one) merges in the True One.
O mind, obtain the treasure of the Naam;
accept the will of your Guru.
When the filth within is removed through the Guru's Shabad,
the pure Naam comes to dwell in the mind.
Led astray by doubt, the world wanders about;
it dies and is born, and Jam (the messenger of Death) brings it to ruin.
O Nanak, fortunate are those who have meditated on the Name of the Lord
and, by the Guru's grace, have enshrined (it) in the mind. ॥4॥
560.3: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Haumai is opposed to the Name; the two do not dwell in one place.
In Haumai (his) service cannot be done, and so the mind goes to waste.
O my mind, remember the Lord; live by the Guru's Shabad.
If you obey the Hukam, then the Lord is met, and then Haumai goes from within.
Haumai fills the whole body; through Haumai (one) comes to birth.
Haumai is a great darkness; in Haumai no one can understand.
In Haumai devotion cannot be done, and the Hukam is not understood.
In Haumai the soul is in bondage; the Naam does not come to dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, on meeting the True Guru, Haumai went, and then the True One came to dwell in the mind.
(Then one) lives the truth, abides in the truth, and, serving the True One, merges (in him). ॥4॥
560.4: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 1, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The bed (of the heart) is one, and the one God is the Master (upon it);
through the Guru (the soul-bride) enjoys the Lord, the ocean of peace.
In my mind is the hope of meeting God in love.
The perfect Guru unites (me with) my Beloved; I will be a sacrifice to my Guru again and again.
My body is full of faults;
how can I meet my perfect Beloved?
She who is virtuous has found my Beloved;
those virtues are not in me: how shall I meet (him), O my mother?
I am worn out with trying ever so many means;
O my Lord, protect poor Nanak. ॥4॥
561.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
My Lord God is beautiful, (yet) I have not known (his) worth;
leaving the Lord God, I have been lured by another.
How am I, so ignorant, to meet the Husband?
She who pleases the Husband is the happy soul-bride; she alone, the wise one, meets the Husband.
Faults are in me: how shall I find the Husband?
Many are your loved ones, O Husband; I do not come to your mind.
She who has enjoyed the Husband's love is the good, happy soul-bride;
those virtues are not in me: what am I, the forsaken one, to do?
The happy soul-bride enjoys the Husband's love day after day, for ever;
will he ever clasp me, the luckless one, to his bosom?
You, my Husband, are full of virtues; I am full of faults;
forgive me, the virtueless one, poor Nanak. ॥5॥
561.2: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 2, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In my mind is a great hope, O Lord: how may I obtain the sight of the Lord?
Let me go and ask my True Guru, and, having asked the Guru, teach my foolish mind.
The strayed mind comes to understand through the Guru's Shabad, and meditates on the Lord, Har Har, for ever.
O Nanak, the one on whom my Beloved casts his glance of grace fixes his mind on the Lord's feet.
I put on every kind of dress for the Husband's sake, that I may be pleasing to the True Lord God;
(but) that dear Husband does not turn his eyes to me: how am I to find comfort?
He for whose sake I adorn myself, that Husband of mine is in love with others.
O Nanak, blessed, blessed, blessed is the happy soul-bride who has enjoyed the love of the Husband, the True, the Beautiful.
Let me go and ask the happy soul-bride, beloved of the Husband: how did you find the Husband, my God?
(She answers:) The True Husband cast his glance of grace upon me, (and) I gave up mine and yours.
Make mind, body and soul, all of it, the Lord God's; by this path, O sister, he is met.
O Nanak, (the one) on whom one's own dear God looks with his glance of grace, (that one's) light blends with the Light.
Whoever brings me a message of the Lord God, to him I would give my mind and body;
each day I would fan (him), do (his) service, and carry water to him.
Day after day I would serve that servant of the Lord who recounts (to me) the discourse of the Lord, Har Har.
Blessed, blessed is the Guru, the Guru, the perfect True Guru, who, O Nanak, fulfils the hope held in the mind.
Unite me, O Lord, with the Guru, my friend, meeting whom I may meditate on the Name of the Lord.
Of the Guru, the True Guru, I would ask for talk of the Lord, and, sharing (his) fellowship, sing the Lord's virtues.
Day by day, for ever, I would sing the Lord's virtues; (O Lord,) (my) mind lives on hearing your Name.
O Nanak, at the moment my Master is forgotten, at that moment my soul dies.
All long to see the Lord, (but) he sees (him) to whom he himself grants the sight.
The one on whom my Beloved casts his glance of grace keeps the Lord, Har Har, ever cherished (in the heart).
He alone cherishes the Name of the Lord, Har Har, for ever and ever, who has met my perfect True Guru.
O Nanak, the servant of the Lord and the Lord have become one; by repeating the Lord, (he) has blended into the Lord. ॥6॥
562.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 1, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Most lofty is his court;
(he) has no end, no near shore or far.
Though one run about millions, millions, millions and hundreds of thousands of times,
one does not reach his mansion, not by a sesame seed's breadth.
Which is that lovely (hour), that moment, in which God is met?
Hundreds of thousands of devotees worship him,
hundreds of thousands of great ascetics practise nothing but austerity,
hundreds of thousands of great yogis practise Yoga,
hundreds of thousands of great enjoyers enjoy (his) pleasures.
(O God,) you dwell in every heart, (but) few know (it).
Is there some friend who would tear away the veil (between me and God)?
I strive, that he may be kind (to me);
to him I would give my soul in sacrifice.
Wandering and wandering, I came to the Sants;
(they) wiped out all my sorrow and doubt.
God called (me) into his mansion, (and) I partook of the Amrit.
Says Nanak, my God is lofty. ॥4॥
562.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Blessed is that moment in which the sight (of God) is beheld;
I am a sacrifice to the True Guru's feet.
O Giver of life, my Beloved God,
(my) mind lives by remembering (your) Name, O God.
Your teaching is true, (your) Bani is Amrit;
O cool and soothing Being, (your) gaze discerns all.
Your Hukam is true; you are seated (for ever) on the throne.
My God, the Imperishable, neither comes nor goes.
You are kind; we are (your) lowly servants.
O Nanak, the Master fills every place and pervades all. ॥4॥
562.3: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you are infinite; only a rare one knows (you);
by the Guru's grace some (rare one) recognises (you) through the Shabad.
This is (your) servant's prayer, O Beloved:
may I live by meditating on your feet, O God.
O merciful Being, my God, the Giver,
he alone has known you to whom you give the understanding.
Ever and for ever I am a sacrifice (to you);
in this world and the next I look to your shelter.
I, the virtueless one, have known nothing of (your) goodness;
O Nanak, beholding the Saadh (the Guru), the mind is dyed (in your love). ॥4॥
563.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That perfect God is the knower of hearts;
(he) bestows the dust (of the feet) of the Saadh as (his) gift.
Show grace, O God, merciful to the meek;
your shelter (is mine), O all-pervading Gopal (the Lord who sustains all).
(God) fills the water, the land and the sky;
God dwells near; he is not far.
The one on whom (he) casts his glance of grace meditates (on him),
and at all hours sings the Lord's virtues.
Nanak has sought (his) refuge at the Lord's door. ॥4॥
563.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you are the great Giver, the knower of hearts;
O all-pervading God, my Master, you pervade all.
O my Beloved God, (your) Name is (my) support;
I live by hearing your Name again and again.
(I have come to) your refuge, O my perfect True Guru;
through the dust (of the feet) of the Sants the mind becomes pure.
(Your) lotus feet I have enshrined in my heart, in (my) bosom;
I am a sacrifice to the sight of you.
Have mercy, that I may sing your virtues,
and that Nanak may find peace repeating the Naam. ॥4॥
563.3: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) the Lord's Amrit is drunk;
(then) the soul neither dies nor ever wastes away.
It is by great good fortune that the perfect Guru is found;
through the Guru's grace one meditates on God.
The Lord (is) jewels, gems, pearls and rubies;
remembering God again and again, (people) have been filled with joy.
Look where I may, (it is) in the refuge of the Saadh (that)
the mind is made pure by singing the Lord's virtues.
My Master dwells within every heart;
Nanak has received the Naam, (for) God has been pleased. ॥4॥
563.4: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Never slip from (my mind), O God, merciful to the meek;
(I am in) your refuge, O all-pervading, compassionate One.
Where you come to mind, that place is beautiful;
the moment you are forgotten, a sigh of grief strikes.
(All) beings are yours; you are ever (their) companion;
give (us your) hand and pull (us) out of the world-ocean.
Coming and going (birth and death) you yourself have made;
the one you protect comes to no sorrow.
You alone are the Master; there is no other (like you), none;
Nanak makes (this) prayer with joined hands. ॥4॥
563.5: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) when you make (yourself) known, then someone knows (you),
and utters the Name you have given.
You are wondrous; your creation fills (one) with awe.
You yourself are the cause, you yourself the creation;
by (your) Hukam is birth, by (your) Hukam death.
Your Name is what supports (my) mind and body;
Nanak, your servant, (looks for) your grace. ॥3॥
564.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 2, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Within me is a longing to meet (him), O dear one; how shall I find the perfect Guru?
Though a child be given a hundred games to play, it cannot do without milk;
the hunger within me does not leave, O friend, though a hundred dishes be set before me.
In my mind and body is love for the Beloved; without the sight (of him), how can the mind be at peace?
Listen, my friend, my dear brother: unite me with the friend who gives peace.
He knows all the pain of my soul, and daily tells (me) of the Lord.
I cannot live a moment without him (God), just as the chatrik (rain-bird) cries out for water.
(O God,) which of your virtues shall I recall and cherish? You keep me, the virtueless, safe.
I have grown forlorn for my Husband, O friend; when shall I see that Husband with my eyes?
All the enjoyment of pleasures is forgotten; without the Husband (they are) of no account.
This garment gives my body no comfort; I cannot put on finery.
To those friends who have enjoyed the love of the dear Beloved I bow.
I put on every adornment, O friend, (but) without the Husband they were of no use.
When the Husband has not asked after (me), O friend, then all (my) youth goes to waste.
Blessed, blessed are those happy soul-brides, O friend, within whom the Husband abides.
To those happy soul-brides, O friend, I am a sacrifice; I would ever wash their feet.
So long as the delusion of another lasted, O friend, so long did I take God to be far off.
When the perfect True Guru was met, O friend, then every hope and wish was fulfilled.
I have found the peace above all peace, O friend; the Husband fills all.
Servant Nanak has enjoyed the Lord's love, O friend, clinging to the feet of the Guru, the True Guru. ॥5॥
564.2: Raag Vadhans, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(Within me are) the true Bani, the strain of the True (Name), and reflection on the Shabad of the True One;
day and night (I) praise the True One: blessed, blessed is my great fortune.
O my mind, be a sacrifice to the True Name.
If you remain the servant of (the Lord's) servants, you will obtain the True Name.
The tongue steeped in the True One is true, and body and mind become true.
Praising another than the True One, you will depart having lost your whole life.
One whose farming is the True (Name), whose sowing is the True (Name), whose trade is true,
earns day and night the profit of the wealth of the True Name, and (his) storehouses brim with devotion.
The True (Name) for food, the True (Name) for clothing, and the Lord's Name, the True One, for support:
these come to one whom (the Lord) forgives, and he finds a place in (the Lord's) mansion.
They come (absorbed) in the True One and go (absorbed) in the True One, and are never cast into births again.
The Gurmukhs are found true at the door of the True One, and merge in the True One.
Their inner being is true, their mind is true, and true is the praise and glory (they sing);
in the true place they praise the True One; I am a sacrifice to the True Guru.
True (and fruitful) is that hour, true that moment, in which there is love for the True One;
(then) one sees the True One, speaks the True One, and the whole visible creation is true (to him).
O Nanak, only when the True One unites (one with himself) is (he) met; he himself brings (one) into union.
As it pleases him, so he keeps (them); he himself gives the command. ॥8॥
565.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The mind runs about in the ten directions; how is it to sing the Lord's praises?
The urge of the senses has it greatly in its grip, and lust and anger torment it every day.
In Sahaj (God's) virtues are dwelt on, with praise, Waah Waah;
the Name of Ram is hard to come by in this age; through the Guru's teaching the Lord's essence is drunk.
When, recognising the Shabad, the mind becomes pure, then it sings the Lord's praises.
When through the Guru's teaching one recognises one's own self, then one finds a dwelling in one's own home (within).
O my mind, ever steeped in (his) love, sing the Lord's praises for ever.
The Lord is pure, ever the giver of peace; obtain (from him) the fruit your mind longs for.
We, the lowly, have become exalted in the Lord's refuge.
He has pulled out the sinking stone; true is his glory.
From poison (we) have become Amrit, having gained understanding through the Guru's teaching.
From the akk (a bitter wild shrub) we have become fragrant sandal; fragrance has been made to dwell within.
Human birth is hard to come by; coming into the world, (that one alone) has earned (the profit)
who by perfect fortune meets the True Guru and meditates on the Lord's Name.
The manmukhs, gone astray, cling to poison, and have wasted this precious life.
The Lord's Name is ever an ocean of peace, (yet) the true Shabad has not pleased them.
With the mouth everyone says Har Har; rare is the one who has enshrined (him) in the heart.
O Nanak, those in whose hearts (the Lord) has come to dwell have attained liberation and release. ॥8॥
565.2: Raag Vadhans, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Having defiled the body with falsehood, why bathe (at places of pilgrimage)?
That one alone is accepted as bathed, when truth is practised.
When truth is within, one becomes true; then the True One is found.
Without what (God) has written there is no understanding; by talking and talking (life) is lost.
Wherever one goes to sit, one should speak what is good, and have the Shabad inscribed in one's consciousness.
Having defiled the body with falsehood, why bathe (at places of pilgrimage)?
I spoke the word (of your praise) only when you made me speak it.
The Amrit Name of the Lord has become dear to my mind.
The Name has come to taste sweet to the mind, and pain has pulled down its camp.
Peace came to dwell in the mind when you gave the command.
The glance of grace is yours, the prayer is mine, O you who brought yourself into being.
I spoke the word (of your praise) only when you made me speak it.
The Master grants each his turn (of life) by the deeds he has done.
Call no one bad, and do not start a quarrel.
Pick no quarrel with the Master; (so) you only bring ruin on yourself.
Having made a rival of the One whose company you must keep, what use is it to go (to him) and weep?
What he gives is to be borne; (what you would say) is to be said to your own mind, not voiced aloud in complaint.
The Master grants each his turn (of life) by the deeds he has done.
He himself has created all, and he himself casts his glance of grace.
No one asks for the bitter; all ask for the sweet.
Let everyone ask for the sweet and see: the Master does what pleases him.
Acts of merit, gifts in charity, many deeds: none of it is equal to the Name, or matches it.
O Nanak, those who have received the Name were shown grace long ago, from the very beginning.
He himself has created all, and he himself casts his glance of grace. ॥4॥
566.1: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) show mercy, that I may utter your Name.
You yourself have created all, and you yourself pervade all.
You yourself pervade all; having created (beings), you have set them to their toil.
Some you yourself have made kings; others you have sent wandering to beg.
Greed and attachment you have made sweet; in this delusion (the world) has gone astray.
Show your mercy always; only then can I utter the Name.
Your Name is true, and is ever dear to my mind.
Pain has gone, and peace has come to dwell (in me).
Gods and men, the refined and the wise, sing (of you);
gods and men, the refined and the wise, those who are pleasing to your mind, sing (of you).
Bewitched by Maya, (others) do not remember (you), and waste this precious life.
Some, dull and foolish, never remember (you) at all; whoever has come must go.
Your Name is ever true; it alone is dear to my mind.
Lovely is your hour (when you are remembered); your Bani is Amrit.
(Your) servants serve (you) with love; those mortals have come to know the taste (of the Name).
Those mortals alone have come to know the taste who have received the Amrit.
Those who are steeped in your Name rise higher every day.
Not one rite, religious duty or discipline (avails), so long as I do not recognise the One.
Ever lovely is your hour (when you are remembered); your Bani is Amrit.
I am a sacrifice to (your) True Name.
Your rule never passes away.
Your rule is ever unshakeable; it never passes away.
He alone is your servant who stays merged in Sahaj.
No enemy, no pain touches him at all, and sin does not come near.
May I ever be a sacrifice to your one Name.
In age after age (there have been) your devotees,
who sing your praise, O Master, at your door,
and repeat (the Name of) the one True Murari (the Lord).
They repeat (the Name of) the True Murari only when you make (it) dwell in their minds;
doubt and delusion are of your making, (and they repeat it) when you take this away.
By the Guru's grace show (us) mercy, and save (us) from Jam.
In age after age (there have been) your devotees.
O my great Master, unseen and infinite,
how am I to make my prayer (to you)? I do not know how to speak.
If you cast your glance of grace, then I recognise the True One.
I recognise your Truth only when you yourself give understanding;
you have made pain and hunger in the world, and (you) take this dread away.
Nanak prays: dread goes when one understands through reflection on the Guru's word.
He himself is the great Master, unseen and infinite.
Your eyes are beautiful, your teeth delightful;
lovely is your nose, and long your hair.
(Your) body is golden, cast in gold.
Cast in gold, (wearing) Krishna's garland: meditate (on him), O friends.
(So that) you need not stand at Jam's door, hear this counsel, O brides.
The heron of herons becomes the swan of swans, (when) the scum of the mind comes off.
(Your) eyes are beautiful, (your) teeth delightful.
Lovely is your gait, sweet your speech.
(It is as) the koels' cooing; lively is (your) youth.
Lively youth is pleasing to you yourself; the wish of (your own) mind is fulfilled.
Like an elephant (saarang) he sets down his foot with a stately sway, rapt in himself.
She who is steeped in Sri Rang (the Lord of Lakshmi) moves about rapt, like the waters of the Ganga.
Nanak, the Lord's servant, prays: lovely is your gait, sweet your speech. ॥8॥
567.1: Raag Vadhans, Chhants, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Steeped in the love of your own Husband, dear one, you are a bride full of glory;
you stay merged in the true Shabad, dear one, and for (your) love and affection the Husband delights in you.
Dear (to him) for her true love, adorned by her Husband, she has formed a bond of love with the Lord, Har Har.
When she shed her self-conceit, then she found the Husband, and merged in the Guru's Shabad.
That soul-bride, made beautiful by the Shabad, is drawn by love; within her is a dear affection.
O Nanak, the Husband himself has united that soul-bride (with himself); the True King has adorned her.
O bride without virtue, see the Husband present before you.
For those who through the Guru have enjoyed (his) love, dear one, the Husband pervades all, filling everything.
The Husband pervades all, filling everything: see him present before you; in every age the One alone is known.
The bride, young and innocent, enjoys the Husband's love in Sahaj; she has met the One who shapes (each) by their deeds.
She who has tasted the Lord's essence, and through the Shabad has sung (his praise) well, abides wholly in the Lord's pool.
O Nanak, that bride pleases the Husband who, through the Shabad, stays in his presence.
Go, dear one, and ask the happy soul-brides who have shed their self-conceit from within.
Those who have not shed their self-conceit from within, dear one, have not grasped the Husband's Hukam.
Those who have shed their self-conceit have found the Husband; (each) enjoys delight in his love.
Ever steeped in (his) love, rapt in Sahaj, she utters the Name day and night.
Fortunate is that bride: her attention is fixed (on him) within, and the Lord's love has become dear to her.
O Nanak, the bride who has made truth her adornment is steeped (in his love) in Sahaj.
Subdue your Haumai, dear one, and walk in the Guru's will.
(So) you will ever enjoy the love of the Lord, your Husband, dear one, finding a dwelling in your own home (within).
Finding a dwelling in her own home, she makes the Shabad resound, and is a wife happy in her Husband for ever.
The Husband is full of delight, his youth ever fresh; day and night the Husband keeps her adorned.
The Lord, her Husband, is her wedded bliss; good fortune is on her forehead; the true Shabad makes her beautiful.
O Nanak, the bride is steeped in the Lord's love when she walks in the True Guru's will. ॥4॥
568.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through the Guru, all trade is good, if it is done in Sahaj.
Let the Name be uttered day and night, and the Lord's essence drunk: (this is) the profit.
The Lord's essence is taken as the profit, the Lord is enjoyed, (when one) utters the Name day and night;
as he gathers virtues, (his) faults are sold off, and he comes to know his own self.
Through the Guru's teaching great glory has been gained; through the true Shabad the essence (of the Name) is drunk.
O Nanak, devotion to the Lord is wondrous; rare is the one who, through the Guru, performs it.
Through the Guru, let the crop of the Lord be sown within, and let the Lord be made to sprout in the body.
Within your own home, savour the essence, and earn the profit for the world beyond.
The one who enshrines the Lord in his mind (earns) the profit for the world beyond; blessed is (such) farming and trade.
He meditates on the Lord's Name, enshrines it in his mind, and understands through reflection on the Guru's word.
The manmukhs have worn themselves out farming and trading, (yet) their craving and hunger do not go.
Says Nanak: sow the Name within the mind, with love, through the true Shabad.
They alone take up the Lord's trade on whose forehead is the jewel of great fortune.
Through the Guru's teaching (their) mind has come to dwell in its own home, and through the true Shabad (comes) detachment.
Good fortune is on their face and forehead; their detachment is in the True One; steeped in the True One, they are given to reflection.
Without the Name the whole world is crazed; (they) have subdued Haumai through the Shabad.
Attached to the true Shabad, wisdom wells up; through the Guru the Name is (their) wedded bliss.
O Nanak, through the Shabad the destroyer of fear is met; one with good fortune on the forehead enjoys the Lord.
Farming and trade are all (his) Hukam; in accepting the Hukam lies glory.
Through the Guru's teaching the Hukam is understood; by the Hukam (he) unites (one) in union (with himself).
United by the Hukam, (one) merges in Sahaj; the Guru's Shabad is infinite.
True glory is gained from the Guru; the True One is the one who adorns.
The destroyer of fear is found when self-conceit is shed; through the Guru (he) unites (one) in union.
Says Nanak: the Name of the Immaculate One, inaccessible and beyond the reach of the senses, pervades all by (his) Hukam. ॥4॥
569.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O my mind, ever keep the True One cherished (in your heart).
(So) you will dwell in peace in your own home (within), and Jamkaal (death) cannot touch you.
Death, its net and Jam cannot so much as look at one who fixes his attention on the true Shabad;
ever steeped in the True One, (his) mind is pure, and (his) coming and going comes to an end.
In the love of another and in doubt the manmukh (world) is ruined, held fast in attachment by Jamkaal.
Says Nanak: listen, O my mind, ever keep the True One cherished (in your heart).
O my mind, within you is the treasure; do not seek the thing outside.
Take for your food whatever pleases (God), and through the Guru behold with (inner) sight.
Through the Guru behold with (inner) sight, O my mind: within (you) is the Lord's Name, your friend.
The manmukhs are blind, empty of (spiritual) wisdom; in the love of another they are led astray.
Without the Name no one is set free; all (the world) is bound by Jamkaal.
Says Nanak: within you is the treasure; do not seek the thing outside.
O my mind, having obtained the precious gift of (human) birth, some have taken up the trade in the True One;
they serve their own True Guru, and within (them) is the Shabad of the Infinite.
Within (them) is the Shabad of the Infinite, and the Lord's Name is dear (to them); in the Name itself they have obtained the nine treasures.
The manmukhs are caught in attachment to Maya and tormented by pain; in (the love of) another they have lost their honour.
(Those who,) subduing Haumai, merge in the true Shabad are steeped deeply in the True One.
O Nanak, a human birth is hard to come by; the True Guru has given (them) this understanding.
O my mind, those who serve their own True Guru are people of great good fortune.
Those who subdue their own mind are the detached.
Those people are detached, their attention fixed on the True One; they have recognised their own self.
Their understanding is steady and most deeply dyed; through the Guru, in Sahaj, they have uttered the Name.
Some are devoted to women and in love with attachment to Maya; (such) unfortunate manmukhs remain asleep.
O Nanak, those who serve their own Guru in Sahaj are fortunate in full measure. ॥4॥
569.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Priceless jewels are traded (by those to whom) the True Guru has given understanding;
(Their) profit and gain is devotion to the Lord; in (his) virtues (they) merge in the Lord of virtues.
He to whom (God) himself gives understanding merges, in (his) virtues, in the Lord of virtues; in the world (he earns) the profit of devotion.
Without devotion there is no peace, and in (the love of) another honour is lost; through the Guru's teaching (he makes) the Name his support.
The merchandise of the Name is gain for ever (to him) whom (God) sets to this trade.
Priceless jewels are traded when the True Guru gives understanding.
Attachment to Maya is pain, all of it; this trade is false.
Speaking falsehood, poison is eaten, and the vices grow many.
The vices grow many, this world is (all) anxiety, and without the Name honour is lost.
Reading and reading, the pandits expound their disputes; without understanding there is no peace.
(Their) coming and going never ends; attachment to Maya is dear (to them).
Attachment to Maya is pain, all of it; this trade is false.
The false and the genuine are all tested in that court of the True One.
The false are thrown out of the Lord's court; standing, they cry out.
Standing, they cry out, the foolish and the ignorant, who as manmukhs have wasted their life.
Maya, the poison that has led the world astray, (so beguiled them that) the True Name did not please (them).
Bearing enmity towards the Sants, the manmukh world earns pain.
The false and the genuine are tested in that true court.
(God) himself does (all); to whom else should one speak? Nothing else can be done.
To whatever (task) pleases him he will set (each one), as befits his greatness.
As befits his greatness, he himself causes (all) to be done; no one is (of himself) a hero, and no one a weakling.
The Life of the world, the Giver, the Maker (of beings) according to (their) deeds: he himself forgives.
By the Guru's grace self-conceit is shed; O Nanak, through the Name honour is gained.
(God) himself does (all); to whom else should one speak? Nothing else can be done. ॥4॥
570.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Lord's Name is the true merchandise, the true trade.
Through the Guru's teaching the Lord's Name is traded; its price is exceedingly great.
Exceedingly great is the worth of the trade in Truth; the fortunate have taken up this true trade.
Within and without they are steeped in devotion, their attention fixed on the True Name.
He alone on whom (God) casts his glance of grace finds the True One, reflecting through the Guru's Shabad.
O Nanak, those steeped in the Name, they alone have found peace in the trade of the True One.
Haumai and Maya are filth; (the mind) is smeared with the filth of Maya.
Through the Guru's teaching the mind is pure; with the tongue one should drink the Lord's sweet essence.
With the tongue one should drink the Lord's sweet essence; (then) the heart is drenched, and through the true Shabad it comes to reflect.
Within is a little well, full of Amrit; through the Shabad the water-drawer (the attention) draws (from it) and drinks.
He alone on whom (God) casts his glance of grace is joined to the True One; with the tongue one should remember the Lord.
O Nanak, those steeped in the Name are pure; the rest are smeared with the filth of Haumai.
