The pandits and the astrologers, all of them, read and read and shout aloud; to whom are they crying out?
Within (them) is attachment to Maya, and filth clings (to them); (theirs) are the dealings of Maya.
The dealings of Maya are dear to the world; in coming and going it suffers pain.
The worm of poison clings to poison, and is sunk in filth.
What is written from the start, that alone (a being) acts out; there is no one to erase it.
O Nanak, those steeped in the Name have found peace for ever; the other fools, the ignorant, have died shouting.
The mind is dyed in attachment to Maya; in attachment (it) has no awareness at all.
If through the Guru this mind is dyed, the colour of another departs.
The colour of another departs, (the mind) merges in the True One, and (its) storehouses are filled with Truth.
He alone who becomes Gurmukh understands (this); the Adorner adorns (him) with Truth.
He whom (God) himself unites, he meets the Lord; nothing more can be said.
O Nanak, without the Name (the world) is led astray in doubt; some, having taken on (his) love, are steeped in the Name. ॥4॥
571.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O my mind, the world is a coming and going; in the end, release is in the True One.
(When) the True One himself forgives, then there is no further round (of birth and death).
Then there is no further round; in the end, release is in the True One; through the Guru, glory is received.
Steeped in the love of the True One, rapt in Sahaj, they remain absorbed in Sahaj.
The True One has become pleasing to their mind, and they have enshrined the True One; steeped in the Shabad, in the end they find release.
O Nanak, those steeped in the Name merge in the True One; never again (do they make) a round in the world-ocean.
Attachment to Maya is madness, all of it; in the love of another (the world) is led astray.
Mother, father: all of it is attachment; (the world) is entangled in attachment itself.
It is entangled in attachment by what it earned before; no one can erase that.
He who fashioned the creation, having made it, watches over it; there is no other as great as he.
The blind manmukh burns and burns and wastes away; without the Shabad, peace has not come (to him).
O Nanak, without the Name everyone has gone wrong; in attachment to Maya (the world) is led astray.
Seeing this world burning, (I) have run to the Lord's refuge.
I offer a prayer before the perfect Guru: save (me), grant (me) glory.
Keep (me) in your refuge, (grant me) the glory of the Lord's Name; no other giver is your equal.
Those set to (your) service are of great good fortune; they have known the One (who is) in every age.
(One may) practise continence, truthfulness, self-restraint and (such) deeds, (but) without the Guru the (high) state of liberation is not attained.
O Nanak, (God) gives understanding of the Shabad to him who goes and falls into the Lord's refuge.
The understanding the Lord gives, that alone wells up; there is no other understanding.
Within and without, you alone are; you yourself give understanding.
You yourself give understanding, and no other (understanding) pleases; through the Guru (the soul) has tasted the Lord's sweet essence.
At the True One's door he is ever true who has sung (his) praise through the true Shabad.
Within the home (of his heart) he has found his own true home; the True Guru gives (him) glory.
O Nanak, those who are steeped in the Name, they alone reach (the Lord's) mansion; that understanding (of theirs) is approved by the True One. ॥4॥
572.1: Raag Vadhans, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
In my mind, in my mind, the True Guru has instilled love.
He has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Har Har, dwell in my mind.
He has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, dwell in my mind, (the Name) that takes away all pains.
By great good fortune (I) have had the sight of the Guru; blessed, blessed is my True Guru.
Rising and sitting, (I) serve the True Guru, by serving whom peace has been found.
In my mind, in my mind, love for the True Guru has been instilled.
I live, I live: seeing the True Guru, (my mind) is filled with delight.
(The Guru) implants the Lord's Name, the Lord's Name (in me); repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (my mind) blossoms.
Repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the lotus (of the heart) has bloomed; (I) have obtained the Lord's Name, the nine treasures.
The sickness of Haumai has gone and the pain has lifted; in Sahaj, (my) Samadhi (deep absorption) is fixed on the Lord.
From the True Guru (I) have obtained the glory of the Lord's Name; touching (the feet of) the divine True Guru, the mind has found peace.
I live, I live: seeing the True Guru, (my mind) is filled with delight.
Should someone bring (him), someone bring and unite (me with) my perfect True Guru,
(then) I would give my mind and body, my mind and body to him, cutting up my body (for him).
My mind and body, cut piece by piece, I would give to him who lets me hear the True Guru's words.
Bairag (longing for the Lord) has arisen in my mind; the longing (mind), meeting the Guru, finds peace in the sight of him.
O Lord, Har Har, giver of peace, show mercy: give me the dust of the True Guru's feet.
Should someone bring (him), someone bring and unite (me with) my perfect True Guru!
For me there is no other giver equal to the Guru, equal to the Guru.
(The Guru) gives the gift of the Lord, the gift of the Lord, who is the Purakh, the all-pervading Being, Niranjan (free of the stain of Maya).
Those who have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har: their pain, doubt and fear have fled.
In the spirit of a servant, the fortunate ones whose minds are fixed on the Guru's feet have met (the Lord).
Says Nanak: the Lord himself unites (them); meeting the True Guru, the Purakh, there is peace.
For me there is no other giver equal to the Guru, equal to the Guru. ॥4॥
572.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Without the Guru I, without the Guru I am utterly without honour.
The world's Life, the world's Life, the Giver: through union with the Guru I have merged (in him).
The True Guru united (me), and I merged in the Lord's Name; repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, I have meditated (on him).
He for whom I went searching and searching, that Friend, the Lord, I have found in (my own) home.
With an undivided gaze I have known the Lord as the One; I have recognised the Lord who pervades every soul (Atam Ram).
Without the Guru I, without the Guru I am utterly without honour.
Those who have found the True Guru, who have found the True Guru, the Lord God brings into union (with himself).
Their feet, their feet I serve; I cling to their feet.
O Lord, Har Har, I serve the feet of those who have meditated on the True Guru, the Purakh, on God.
You are the great Giver, the knower of hearts; fulfil my longing, O Lord, my King.
In union with the Gursikhs my longing is fulfilled, and night and day (I) sing the Lord's praises.
Those who have found the True Guru, who have found the True Guru, the Lord God brings into union (with himself).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the Gursikh, my beloved friend,
who lets me hear the Lord's Name, the Lord's Name; the Name is my Beloved, (my) mainstay.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the friend of my life-breath; without it I do not live for a moment, not for the blink of an eye.
(If) the Lord, Har Har, the giver of peace, shows mercy, (then) through the Guru I drink the Amrit.
The Lord himself instils the longing and unites (the soul with himself); the Lord himself, of himself, adorns (it).
I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, to the Gursikh, my beloved friend.
The Lord himself, the Lord himself is that Purakh, Niranjan.
The Lord himself, the Lord himself unites (the soul with himself); what he does, that comes to be.
What pleases the Lord God, that alone comes to be; nothing else can be done.
By great cleverness (he) cannot be won; all have tried their cleverness and grown weary.
By the Guru's grace servant Nanak has seen (him): for me there is none other than the Lord.
The Lord himself, the Lord himself is that Purakh, Niranjan. ॥4॥
573.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Lord, unite me with the True Guru, with the True Guru; O Lord, the True Guru's feet are dear to me.
The darkness of ignorance is gone, for the Guru has put the salve of the Guru's wisdom (in my eyes).
The True Guru has applied the salve of the Guru's wisdom, and the darkness of ignorance has been destroyed.
By serving the True Guru I have reached the highest state; I have repeated (the Name of) the Lord with each breath and each mouthful.
Those to whom the Lord God has shown grace, he has joined to the True Guru's service.
O Lord, unite me with the True Guru, with the True Guru; O Lord, the True Guru's feet are dear to me.
My True Guru, my True Guru is dear (to me); I cannot live without the Guru.
He gives (me) the Lord's Name, the Lord's Name, my companion at the last.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is my companion at the last; the Guru, the True Guru, has made the Name firm (within me).
Where no son, no wife, no friend (stands by), there the Name of the Lord, Har Har, has set (me) free.
Blessed, blessed is the True Guru, the Purakh, Niranjan, meeting whom I meditate on the Lord's Name.
My True Guru, my True Guru is dear (to me); I cannot live without the Guru.
Those who have not gained the sight, the sight of the True Guru, the Purakh,
fruitless, fruitless is their life; they have wasted it all in vain.
They have wasted their life for nothing; those Saakats (who have turned from God) are dead, and dying, they pine.
Though the jewel, the precious thing, is in their own home, they go hungry; those luckless ones are far from the Lord.
For the Lord's sake, never look upon those who have not meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har,
those who have not gained the sight, the sight of the True Guru, the Purakh.
I am a humble chatrik, a chatrik; this is my prayer to the Lord:
unite me with the Guru, my Beloved, so that, meeting the Guru, I may worship the True Guru.
I can worship the True Guru and the Lord, Har Har, (only) when the Lord God shows grace.
I have no friend other than the Guru; the Guru, the True Guru, is my life itself.
Says Nanak, within me the Guru has made the Naam firm: the Name of the Lord, Har Har, the ever-true Lord.
I am a humble chatrik, a chatrik; (this) is my prayer to the Lord. ॥4॥
574.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
O Lord, show grace, show grace: unite (me) with the True Guru, the giver of peace.
I would ask, I would ask the True Guru about the Lord.
I would ask the True Guru about the Lord, (the Guru) who has gained the treasure of the Naam.
I would fall at (his) feet and pray to (him) every day; the Guru, the True Guru, has shown the way.
He alone is a devotee who knows pain and pleasure as one and the same, and is steeped in the Name of the Lord, Har Har, in the Lord.
O Lord, show grace, show grace: unite (me) with the Guru, the True Guru, the giver of peace.
Listen through the Guru, listen through the Guru: by the Name, Haumai and all sins are destroyed.
Repeat the Lord, Har Har, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: (by it) the fevers of the world have come off.
Those who have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have had their pains and sins taken away.
The True Guru has put the sword of wisdom in (their) hand, and (with it) they have struck down and destroyed Jam's servants.
The Lord God, the giver of peace, has shown grace, and pains, sins and torments have gone.
Listen to the Name through the Guru, listen through the Guru: Haumai and all sins are destroyed.
Repeat the Lord, Har Har, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: (that Name) has become dear to my mind.
Repeating (it) with the mouth through the Guru, with the mouth through the Guru, (one) has driven out all ailments.
Repeating (it) through the Guru, (one) has driven out all ailments, and the body has become whole.
Night and day the Samadhi of Sahaj stays fixed on the Lord, for (one) has repeated the Lord, the deep and profound.
Whoever has meditated on the Naam, of (high) caste or of no caste, has gained the supreme treasure.
Repeat the Lord, Har Har, repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har: (that Name) has become dear to my mind.
Show grace, O Lord, show grace, O Lord; in your grace, save (me).
I am a sinner, I am a sinner, without virtue, lowly, (but) yours.
I, a sinner, without virtue, lowly, (but) yours, have come to your refuge, O merciful Lord.
You are the breaker of sorrows, the giver of all peace; I, a stone, have crossed over, ferried across by you.
Meeting the True Guru, (I) have found the savour of the Lord; the Name has saved servant Nanak.
Show grace, O Lord, show grace, O Lord; in your grace, save (me). ॥4॥
575.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghorian, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
This body is a fine mare, dear ones, created by the Lord.
Blessed is the human birth; (this body) is gained through merit.
The human birth is gained through great merit; that body is golden and lovely,
which, through the Guru, takes on the deep crimson dye, dyed afresh with the Lord, Har Har Har.
This body is beautiful, for through it I repeat the Lord; it is made lovely by the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
(This body) is gained by great good fortune, with the Naam for companion; O servant Nanak, it is the Lord who created it.
Understanding the Good One, I put the saddle on the body;
mounting it, dear ones, I cross the treacherous (world-) ocean.
That treacherous ocean has endless waves; through the Guru, (the Lord) carries (one) across.
Boarding the ship of the Lord, the fortunate one crosses over; the Guru, the boatman, carries (him) across through the Shabad.
Night and day, in the Lord's love, he sings the Lord's virtues; dyed with the Lord, he becomes of the Lord's own colour.
Servant Nanak has attained the state of nirvana, where desire is stilled: the Lord's state, sublime and good.
The bridle in (the mare's) mouth is the wisdom the Guru has made firm (within);
the Lord's love within the body is the whip laid on it.
Laying on the whip of love for the Lord, Har Har, within the body, (one) conquers the mind; through the Guru (alone) is it conquered.
He shapes the unshaped (mind), receives the Shabad, and drinks the Amrit, the Lord's essence.
Hearing with his ears the Bani the Guru has uttered, he has put the Lord's colour on the mare.
The road is long, the path is hard; (the Guru) has brought servant Nanak across it.
The body is a mare, a fine mare, created by the Lord.
Blessed, blessed is that mare through which (one) repeats the Lord God.
That (mare) through which (one) repeats the Lord God is blessed and worthy of praise; it is gained as ordained from the first, by the deeds (of the past) gathered together.
Mount the dear body-mare that carries (you) over the treacherous (ocean), and through the Guru meet the Lord of supreme bliss.
The perfect Lord, Har Har, has arranged the wedding; the Sants have gathered, and the wedding party has come.
Servant Nanak has found the Lord as the Groom; there is rejoicing, and the Sants, gathered together, offer their congratulations. ॥4॥
575.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
This body is a lovely mare, dyed in a new colour by the Lord.
It has begged the Guru for the Guru's wisdom, the wisdom of the Lord.
It begged for wisdom, for the Lord's beautiful discourse, for the Lord's Name, and came to know (his) state and measure.
The Creator has made its whole life fruitful; joined to the Name of the Lord, Ram, it has spoken (of him).
Praising the Name of the Lord, Ram, the Lord's servants have begged the Lord God for the Lord's devotion.
Servant Nanak says: listen, O Sants, devotion to the Lord, Govind, is what is good.
The body (-mare) is golden, its saddle of gold,
studded with the Name of the Lord, Har Har, as its jewel.
Setting (in it) the jewel of the Name, (one) has found Govind; the Lord is met, and with him the Lord's virtues and peace in plenty.
Whoever has received the Guru's Shabad and meditated on the Lord's Name is, by great fortune, coloured with the Lord's colour.
He has met the Lord, the Master, the knower of hearts, the Lord ever new, ever fresh in colour.
Nanak utters (the Name) and knows the Name; he has begged the Lord God for the Lord's Name.
The Guru has put the bridle in (the mare's) mouth and set the elephant-goad (on the mind);
the elephant of the mind has come under control through the Guru's Shabad.
The mind has come under control, the supreme state is reached, and that soul-bride is loved by her Husband.
Within her, love for the Lord has taken hold; the wife of the Lord God shines in his home.
Dyed in the Lord's love, rapt in Sahaj, she has found the Lord God, Har Har.
Servant Nanak, the slave of the Lord, says: (only) the fortunate have meditated on the Lord, Har Har.
The body is the mare, dear ones, through which the Lord is found.
Meeting the True Guru, dear ones, (one) has sung the song of joy.
Singing the Lord's song of joy, the Name of Ram, the servant serves the Lord with a servant's devotion;
he goes and reaches God's palace of joy, and enjoys the delight of the Lord's love.
He sings the virtues of Ram with love in his mind, and, following the Guru's teaching, meditates on the Lord in his mind.
The Lord has shown grace to servant Nanak: mounting the body-mare, he has found the Lord. ॥4॥
576.1: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 4, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Meeting the Guru, dear ones, I have found the dear Lord.
I have given (him) this body and mind, offering them up again and again.
Giving body and mind, I have won over the world-ocean; my subjection to Jam is ended.
I have become steady, I have drunk the Amrit, and (my) coming and going has stopped.
I have found that home and merged in Sahaj; the Lord's Name is (my) support.
Says Nanak, in peace I enjoy delights; I bow to the perfect Guru.
Listen, my dear friend, my companion:
the Guru has given (me) the mantra, the true Shabad.
I have meditated on the true Shabad and sung the song of joy, and the anxieties have left my mind.
I have found that God; (now I) go nowhere else, and ever, ever abide with (him).
Whoever is pleasing to dear God has true honour; God has given him the wealth of the Lord, in Sahaj.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that servant; (O God,) through him all have received your gift.
When it pleased you, (O God,) then (we) were satisfied and filled.
The mind has become cool; all thirst is quenched.
The mind has become cool, the burning (within) is ended, and a great treasure is found.
All the Sikhs and servants have begun to partake (of it); I am a sacrifice to the True Guru.
They have become fearless, dyed in the Master's love, and have put out the fear of Jam.
Nanak is (your) slave, (your) servant ever at (your) side; may I worship you with (my) attention fixed (on you).
(My) hopes and desires are fulfilled, O my dear (Lord).
I am without virtue, dear (Lord); all virtues are yours.
All virtues are yours, my Master; with what mouth shall I praise you?
You weighed none of my merits or faults; you forgave me in a moment.
The nine treasures are mine; congratulations ring out, and the unstruck trumpets play.
Says Nanak, I have found the Husband in my own home; all my sorrows, dear (Lord), have left me. ॥4॥
577.1: What use is listening to falsehood? (False things) go by like gusts of the wind.
O Nanak, accepted are those ears that hear the True Master.
I am a sacrifice through and through to those who have heard God with their ears.
They are at peace in Sahaj who have uttered (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, with the tongue.
They are at peace in Sahaj, priceless in virtue; they have come to carry the world across.
God's feet are the ship across the ocean of fear; (through them) they have carried countless ones across.
Those on whom my Master has shown grace — their account has not been reckoned.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice through and through to the one who has heard God with his ears.
With my eyes I have seen the world, but the thirst is not quenched; it is great in me.
O Nanak, those eyes are of another kind, which see my Beloved.
I am a sacrifice to those who have beheld the Lord God.
They are pleasing in the Lord's true court.
Honoured by the Master, they are foremost, steeped in love for the Lord.
Filled with the Lord's essence, merged in Sahaj, they know the all-pervading Lord in every heart.
They alone are true friends, they are Sants, they are at peace, who are pleasing to their Master.
Says Nanak, to those who have beheld the Lord God I am ever a sacrifice.
Without the Name, the body is in darkness, blind and empty.
O Nanak, his life bears fruit in whose heart the True Master has come to dwell.
I am cut in pieces as a sacrifice to those who have beheld my Lord God.
The Lord's servants have tasted the sweet Amrit of the Lord, Har Har, and are fulfilled.
The Lord is sweet to their minds; God is pleased, the Amrit has rained down, and there is peace.
Sorrow is destroyed and delusion banished from the body by hailing the victory of the Master, the Lord of the world.
They are free of attachment, (their) vices have ceased, and their tie with the five (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride) is broken.
Says Nanak, I am cut in pieces as a sacrifice to those in whose heart my Lord God has come to dwell.
Those whom the Lord wants are alone called (his) servants.
Nanak knows it to be true: the Master is not apart from the Sants.
Water meets water and is blended in;
(the soul's) light has merged with the Light (of God).
The perfect Purakh, the Creator, has taken (it) into himself; he alone, he himself, is known (everywhere).
There, in Sunn (the stillness where no thought stirs) and in Sahaj, Samadhi holds, and the One, the One alone, is spoken of.
He himself is hidden, he himself is unbound; he himself tells of himself.
O Nanak, delusion, fear and the (three) qualities (of Maya) are destroyed; water meets water and is blended in. ॥4॥
578.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O God, Cause of creation, all-powerful,
protect the whole world, giving (it) your hand.
All-powerful Master, able to shelter those who seek refuge, treasure of mercy, giver of peace,
To your servants who have recognised the One, I am a sacrifice.
(Your) colour and sign cannot be perceived; you are beyond all telling.
Nanak prays: hear (my) prayer, O God, Cause of creation, all-powerful.
These beings are yours; you are (their) Creator.
O God, you take away pain, suffering and doubt.
Taking away doubt, pain and suffering in an instant, save (us), O God, merciful to the meek.
(You are) mother, father, master and friend; the whole world is your child, O Gopal.
Whoever comes to (your) refuge obtains the treasure of virtues; he is not born again and does not die.
Nanak, your servant, prays: all beings are yours; you are (their) Creator.
At all hours the Lord is to be meditated on;
(so) the fruit the mind longs for is obtained.
Meditating on God, the mind's desire is obtained, and the terrors of Jam are erased.
(One who) has sung of Gobind in the Saadh Sangat has had (his) hope fulfilled.
Giving up pride, attachment and all vices, one becomes pleasing to God's mind.
Nanak prays: day and night, the Lord, Har Har, is ever to be meditated on.
At (his) door the unstruck music plays;
in every heart the Lord Gobind resounds.
Govind resounds, ever abiding (there), beyond reach, beyond the senses, lofty.
His virtues are endless; nothing can be said (of them), and no one can reach (him).
He himself creates, he himself sustains; he has fashioned all beings and creatures.
Nanak prays: there is peace in the Naam and in devotion; at (his) door the unstruck music plays. ॥4॥
578.2: Raag Vadhans, Ghar 5, Alahniyan, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Blessed is the Creator, the True King, who has set the world to its worldly business.
When the allotted time is up and the cup is full, the dear one is seized and driven off.
The dear one is seized and driven off when the written (order) comes, and all the brothers weep.
Body and swan (the soul) are parted when the days are run out, O my mother.
As was written, so has (each) received, according to what (each) earned before.
Blessed is the Creator, the True King, who has set the world to its worldly business.
Remember the Master, O my brothers; all must make this journey.
Here the false business (of the world) lasts four days; (all) must surely go on ahead.
(All) must surely go on ahead, like guests; why should we be proud?
Let us take the Name of him alone, by serving whom peace is found in (his) court.
Ahead, no one's command holds at all; on each head falls what (each) has done.
Remember the Master, O my brothers; all must make this journey.
Whatever pleases the all-powerful (Lord), that comes to pass; this world is (but) a pretext.
The True Creator pervades the water, the land and the sky.
The True Creator is unseen and infinite; his limit has not been found.
Fruitful is the coming (into the world) of those who have meditated (on him) with a single mind.
He himself tears down, and tearing down builds again; by (his) Hukam he sets (all) right.
Whatever pleases the all-powerful (Lord), that comes to pass; this world is (but) a pretext.
Says Nanak: O brother, that one is known to weep (truly) who weeps with love (for the Lord).
O brother, if one weeps for the sake of worldly goods, all that weeping is in vain.
All that weeping is in vain; the heedless world weeps for the sake of Maya.
It discerns nothing of good and bad, and wastes this body for nothing.
Everyone who has come here shall go; (yet) you act in pride over what is false.
Says Nanak: O brother, that one is known to weep (truly) who weeps with love (for the Lord). ॥4॥
579.1: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Come, my friends, let us meet and take the True Name.
Let us weep over the parting of the body, (and) keep our Master in mind.
Let us keep the Master in mind and watch the road (ahead): we too must go there.
He whose (creature) it was has taken (it back); his will has come to pass.
What (the departed one) did and gathered has come before (him); what command can we give?
Come, my friends, let us meet and take the True Name.
Death should not be called bad, O people, if one knows how to die such a death.
Serve your all-powerful Master, (so that) the road ahead becomes easy.
If you go by the easy road, you will gain the fruit, and ahead you will receive glory.
If you go with the offering (of the Name) and merge in the True One, your honour will be accepted at the reckoning.
You will gain a place in the (Lord's) mansion and be pleasing to the Master; (such a one) enjoys delights in his love.
Death should not be called bad, O people, if anyone knows how to die.
The death of brave men is rightful, if they die approved (by the Lord).
Only those are called brave ahead who are given true honour in (the Lord's) court.
In the court they receive honour, they depart with honour, and ahead no pain touches them.
If they meditate (on him) as the One, they gain the fruit; serving him, fear runs away.
Do not speak proud words; keep within your own mind: the Knower himself knows (all).
The death of brave men is rightful, if they die approved (by the Lord).
Says Nanak: for whom, O brother, should one weep? This world is a play.
The Master watches over what he has made, and gives thought to (his) creation.
He gives thought to (his) creation and gives (it) support; he who made it knows (it).
He himself sees, he himself understands, he himself recognises (his) Hukam.
He who made all (this) alone knows (it); his form is infinite.
Says Nanak: for whom, O brother, should one weep? This world is a play. ॥4॥
580.1: Raag Vadhans Dakhani, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Know the Creator to be true, the eternal; the True One is the Sustainer,
who fashioned his own self by himself, the True One, unseen and infinite.
Joining the two millstones (earth and sky), he set (them) apart; without the Guru there is pitch darkness.
He created the sun and the moon (to light) the day and the night; reflect on (his) wondrous play.
You are the True Master, true; you give true love.
You created the earth; you are the giver of pain and pleasure.
Creating woman and man, (you created) the poison of Maya, attachment and love.
The sources of life and the tongues are yours; you give support to (all) beings.
You have made creation your throne; you settle (all) in truth.
You created coming and going; you, the Maker, are eternal.
Bound in vices, the soul is born and dies, comes and goes.
The wretched one has forgotten the Name; once drowned, what remedy is there for him?
Leaving virtues, he has loaded poison, a trader in faults.
The summons have come for those dear ones, by the Hukam of the True Creator.
Wife and husband are parted; (he alone) unites the parted.
(Jam) does not regard the beauty of the lovely woman; by the Hukam the task is laid on his head.
(Jam's messengers) do not consider child or old; they break bonds of love and affection.
By the Hukam of the True One the nine doors are shut, and the swan has flown to the sky.
The wife is left alone, robbed by falsehood, widowed; the corpse lies in the courtyard at the door.
O mother, at this death my senses have died, (she cries); the wife weeps at the door and the gate.
O brides of the Husband, weep, cherishing the virtues of the True One.
The dear one has been rubbed with water and bathed, and wrapped in clothes of silk.
The true words are raised like music; the five (nearest kin) are as dead, stricken at heart.
Parted from my dear one, it has been my death, (she cries); cursed is living in the world.
That one alone is known (as true) who dies while yet alive, in love and affection for the True Husband.
Weep, you who have come to weep: (you are) robbed by falsehood in the world.
I am robbed, running after worldly business; the Husband has left me, (for my ways are those) of a woman without a lord.
In every home the Husband (is with) the brides who are in love and affection for the Beautiful One.
I must praise my true Husband; I am delighted in the Name of the Husband.
Meeting the Guru, (her) guise is changed: the bride's adornment is the True One.
Come, my friends, let us meet; remember the Creator.
Through the Name the woman becomes a happy soul-bride; the True One is (her) adorner.
Says Nanak: sing no song of separation; (sing) the contemplation of God. ॥8॥
581.1: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
He who created the world and absorbs it (again): know that Master (to be in his) creation.
Do not search for the True One far away; recognise the Shabad in every heart.
Recognise the true Shabad; do not think him far away, who made this creation.
When one meditates on the Naam, then one finds peace; without the Name the contest is lost.
He who established (it) alone knows its way; what can anyone say to describe (it)?
He who established the world and spread the net (over it): accept him as the Master.
O brother, whoever has come must rise and go; the world is (but) a halt midway on the road.
On every head the True One has written pain and pleasure, by the reckoning of (deeds done) before.
He gives pain and pleasure as (each) has done; that goes along with the soul.
(Each) does the deeds the Creator makes him do; he can seek no other work.
He himself is detached; (the world) is bound in worldly business; issuing (his) Hukam, he sets (it) free.
Saying today, tomorrow, one is seized by death; in the love of another, (all one does) is in vain.
On the way of Jam the road cannot be seen; it is a wilderness, pitch dark.
(There is) no water, no quilts or mattresses, no food of any kind.
No food (given) with love, no cold water, no clothes or adornment.
A chain is on his neck, (Jam) stands over his head and strikes (him); no house or home is to be seen.
Seeds sown now do not sprout; he repents, with the load on his head.
Without the True One no one is a friend; this is the true reflection.
O brother, those who weep and repeat (the Name) are honoured, (as is one) who, joining (the Sangat), weeps, cherishing (God's) virtues.
(She who is) robbed by Maya weeps; the weepers weep for worldly business.
(Such a one) weeps for worldly business and does not wash off the filth; the world is (but) a dream.
As at a juggler's show, (she) wanders in doubt and goes astray, robbed by falsehood, in pride.
He himself sets (beings) on the path; he himself does the deeds.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam the Perfect Guru has saved, (and they abide) in Sahaj and in love. ॥4॥
581.2: Raag Vadhans, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O brother, whoever has come must rise and go; this world is a false show.
By serving the True One the true home (is found); (serving) the True One, (one becomes) pure and truthful.
When in falsehood and greed one finds no acceptance (here), ahead too one gets no place.
No one says (to him), come in, be seated; (he is) like a crow at a deserted house.
Birth and death (bring) the great separation; the whole world perishes.
Through greed, worldly business and Maya the world is led astray; Death stands (over it) and makes it weep.
O brother, come, my brothers, let us embrace, and meeting together, let us give blessings.
O brother, union with the True One never ends; let us give blessings for (union with) the Beloved.
Give blessings, and practise devotion; for those (already) united, what (further) union (is there)?
Some have strayed from the Name, from (their true) home and place; through the Guru's Shabad, (remembering) the True One is the (true) game.
(Those) merged in the Shabad do not go by the way of Jam; age after age (they abide) in the True One's form.
O friends and kin, meet with those who join (others to the Lord), who, meeting the Guru, have untied (their) nooses.
O brother, (one) comes naked into the world, with pain and pleasure written as (his) lot.
The written hour (of departure), fixed by what (one) earned before, is not put off.
The True One sat and wrote Amrit or poison; to whatever he attached (him), to that he is attached.
The enchantress (Maya) has cast her spells, (and put) a many-coloured thread round (his) neck.
With shallow understanding the mind has become shallow; he has eaten (Maya's bait) as the fly eats molasses.
Naked he came into the world, and naked he is bound and driven off.
O brother, weep if anyone must weep: the dear one has been bound and sent off.
No one can erase the written lot; from (the Lord's) door the summons has come.
The summons came when it pleased him, and the mourners wept.
Sons, brothers, nephews and the dearest loved ones weep.
(Let one) weep in (God's) fear, cherishing and recalling (his) virtues; no one dies with the dead.
O Nanak, in every age they are known as wise who weep, keeping the True One in mind. ॥4॥
582.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Let us praise God, the True Lord; he is able to do every task, all there is.
That soul-bride never sits as a widow, nor does she ever grieve.
She never grieves; night and day she enjoys delights, that soul-bride, absorbed in (her Husband's) mansion:
she who has known the Beloved, who shapes (each) by their deeds, and who speaks the Amrit word.
The virtuous ones dwell on (his) virtues and keep their Husband cherished (in the heart); separation never befalls them.
Let us praise the True Husband, who is able to do all there is.
The True Master is recognised through the Shabad; he himself unites (one with himself).
That soul-bride is dyed in the Beloved's love who sheds self-conceit from within.
She who sheds self-conceit from within is consumed by death no more; through the Guru she has known the One alone.
The bride's longing has been fulfilled, she is drenched (with love) within; the Giver, the Life of the world, has met her.
Dyed in the love of the Shabad, intoxicated with youth, she rests merged in her Husband's embrace.
The True Master is recognised through the Shabad; he himself unites (one with himself).
I go and ask those Sants who have recognised their own Husband.
Leaving self-conceit, I serve (them); the True Husband is met in Sahaj and in love.
The True Husband comes and meets her who practises Truth; the soul-bride stays dyed in the True Shabad.
She is never a widow, ever a happy soul-bride; within her is the Samadhi of Sahaj.
The Husband pervades everywhere, to the full; see him close at hand, and rejoice in him in Sahaj and in love.
I go and ask those Sants who have recognised their own Husband.
Even we, parted from the Husband, may meet (him), if we cling to the feet of the True Guru, the True One.
The True Guru is ever merciful; he burns away faults through the Shabad.
Burning away faults through the Shabad, he takes away the love of another, and (the soul-bride) is dyed in the True One alone.
Through the True Shabad she has found lasting peace, and (her) Haumai and wandering have gone.
The Husband is pure, ever the giver of peace; O Nanak, (the Guru) unites (one with him) through the Shabad.
Even we, parted from the Husband, may meet (him), if we cling to the feet of the True Guru, the True One. ॥4॥
583.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Listen, O brides of the Husband: serve the Husband, reflecting through the Shabad.
The one full of faults does not know the Husband; forgetting the Husband, she weeps, robbed.
(She who) weeps holding the Husband dear, ever dwelling on (his) virtues: (her) Husband neither dies nor goes away.
Through the Guru she has known (him), through the Shabad recognised (him), and she merges in true love.
She who has not known her Husband, who shapes (each) by their deeds, the false one, is robbed by falsehood.
Listen, O brides of the Husband: serve the Husband, reflecting through the Shabad.
He himself has created all the world; the world is a coming and going.
Through attachment to Maya he has led (it) astray; (the soul-bride) dies and is born again and again.
Dying and being born again and again, her vices grow; devoid of wisdom, she is robbed.
Without the Shabad she did not find the Husband, and has wasted her life; full of faults, the false one weeps.
The Husband is the Life of the world: for whom should one weep? She who forgets the Husband weeps.
He himself has created all the world; the world is a coming and going.
That Husband is true, ever true; he neither dies nor goes away.
The ignorant soul-bride wanders astray; in the love of another, she sits as a widow.
In the love of another she sits as a widow; in attachment to Maya she suffers pain, her span of life shrinks, her body wastes away.
Whatever has come will all go; through the love of another, pain has taken hold.
Jamkaal is not seen; the world quarrels over Maya, and sets its mind on greed and avarice.
That Husband is true, ever true; he neither dies nor goes away.
Some, parted from the Husband, weep; the blind one does not know that the Husband is with (her).
By the Guru's grace the True Husband is met (by her who) ever cherishes (him) within.
(For her who) cherishes the Husband within, he is ever with (her); the manmukh has thought (him) far away.
This body of the one who did not know the Master close at hand is knocked about and wasted, of no use.
O Nanak, that soul-bride, united (by the Guru), meets (him), who keeps the Husband ever cherished within.
Some, parted from the Husband, weep; the blind one does not know that the Husband is with (her). ॥4॥
584.1: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those parted from the Husband weep; my Husband is true, and is ever with (me).
Those who have known for certain that they must depart serve the True Guru, cherishing the Naam.
(For one who) ever cherishes the Naam, the True Guru is with (him); serving the True Guru, (he) has found peace.
Slaying death through the Shabad and enshrining the True One in the heart, (he) has no more coming and going.
True is the Master, true his glory; he watches over (all), looking on with his glance of grace.
Those parted from the Husband weep; my Husband is true, and is ever with (me).
My God, the Master, is higher than all: how am I to meet the dear Beloved?
When the True Guru joined (me to him), I met (him) in Sahaj, and kept the Husband enshrined in (my) heart.
Keeping him ever enshrined in the heart, (I hold) love for the Beloved; through the True Guru the Husband is seen.
The robe of attachment to Maya is of a fleeting dye; wearing it, the foot slips.
The robe dyed in the Husband's love is true (and fast); wearing it, (one) puts thirst away.
My God, the Master, is higher than all: how am I to meet the dear Beloved?
I have recognised God, the True One; any other, full of faults, has gone astray.
My own Husband ever delights in me, as I reflect through the True Shabad.
Reflecting through the True Shabad, the bride is dyed in (his) love; meeting the True Guru, she has found the Beloved.
Within, she is dyed in love, intoxicated in Sahaj; every enemy and every pain has gone.
Let body and mind be given to one's own Guru; then the mind is drenched (with love), and (the Guru) dispels the pains of craving.
I have recognised the Husband, the True One; any other, full of faults, has gone astray.
The True One created the world himself; without the Guru, all is pitch dark.
He himself unites, he himself meets, he himself gives love.
He himself gives love, and the trade (in the Name) in Sahaj; through the Guru he makes (one's) life beautiful.
Blessed is the coming into the world of one who has shed self-conceit; at the door of the True One, (he) is found true.
Through the jewel of wisdom, light has dawned in (his) heart; O Nanak, the Naam is dear (to him).
The True One created the world himself; without the Guru, all is pitch dark. ॥4॥
584.2: Raag Vadhans, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
This body is frail and wearing out; old age comes and overtakes it.
Those whom the Guru has protected are saved; any other dies and is born, comes and goes.
The others die and are born, come and go, and departing at the end, they regret; without the Name there is no peace.
What one earns here, that fruit one receives; the manmukh has lost (his) honour.
In the city of Jam is pitch darkness, deep gloom; there is neither sister nor brother there.
This body is frail and wearing out; old age comes and overtakes it.
Only then does the body become gold, when the True Guru unites (one with the Lord).
(Then) the delusion of Maya is cut away from within, and (one) merges in the True Name.
Merged in the True Name, he sings the Lord's praises, and meeting the Beloved, finds peace.
He stays ever in bliss, day and night, and Haumai leaves (him) from within.
Those who have fixed their mind on the Lord's Name: I fall at their feet.
Only then does the body become gold, when the True Guru unites (one with the Lord).
That True One, the ever-True, is praised (only) if the True Guru grants understanding.
Without the True Guru, (the soul-brides) are led astray by doubt; what face will they show in the world beyond, once they have gone?
Having gone (there), what face can they show? (Each) regrets her faults, and earns pain upon pain.
Those who are imbued with the Name are dyed deep red, and rest merged in the Husband's embrace.
None as great as he is to be seen; before whom (else) should one go and speak?
That True One, the ever-True, is praised (only) if the True Guru grants understanding.
Those who have praised the True One, the ever-True: I fall at their feet.
Those people are true and spotless; meeting them, all filth goes.
Meeting them, all filth goes; (one) bathes in the true pool, and (abides) in the True One, in Sahaj and in love.
The True Guru has given understanding of the Name, immaculate, beyond reach and beyond the senses.
Night and day they perform devotion, dyed in (his) love; O Nanak, they stay merged in the True One.
Those who have meditated on the True One, the ever-True: I fall at their feet. ॥4॥
585.1: Vadhans ki Vaar: by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji); to be sung to the tune of Lalan Behlima.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those dyed in the Shabad, with the True Name enshrined in their hearts, are the great swans;
they gather Truth, and abide ever in the True One, in love with the True Name.
They are ever spotless, no filth clings (to them); the Creator has cast his glance of grace (on them).
I, Nanak, am a sacrifice to those who repeat (the Name of) Murari night and day. ॥1॥
585.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
I took him for a great swan, and so I kept his company;
had I known him to be a wretched heron, I would never have come near him at all. ॥2॥
585.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Seeing the swans swimming, the herons too grew eager;
(but) the wretched herons drowned and died, heads down and feet up. ॥3॥
585.4: (O Lord,) you yourself, you alone, are all there is; you yourself made the root (of creation).
You yourself are the Formless One; there is no other, no second.
You are the Cause of creation, all-powerful; whatever you do comes about.
You give gifts unasked to all beings.
Say, all of you: praise, praise to the True Guru, who has put the gift of the Lord's Name into (our) mouths. ॥1॥
586.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
All that has form is in fear; the dear Lord alone is without fear.
When the True Guru is served, the Lord dwells in the mind; there, fear never comes.
No enemy, no pain comes near him; none can touch him.
The Gurmukh has reflected in the mind: whatever pleases him (the Lord) comes to pass.
O Nanak, he himself will preserve (one's) honour; it is he who sets (one's) affairs right. ॥1॥
586.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Some friends are leaving, some have left; those who remain will go in their turn too.
Those who have not served the True Guru come and go, and regret.
O Nanak, those imbued with the True One are not parted (from him); serving the True Guru, they merge (in him). ॥2॥
586.3: Let us meet that friend, the True Guru, within whom is the Lord, the giver of virtues.
Let us meet that beloved True Guru, who has slain Haumai from within.
Blessed, blessed is that perfect True Guru, who, by giving the Lord's teaching, has set right the whole world.
Repeat ever, O Sants, the Name of Ram, which carries (one) across the poisonous ocean of the world.
The Perfect Guru has given (me) the Lord's teaching; to the Guru I am a sacrifice for ever. ॥2॥
586.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The service and work of the True Guru is the essence of the joy of all joys.
Here (it) brings honours, and in the Lord's court, the door of liberation.
True is the work (one) does, Truth (one's) clothing, the True Name (one's) support.
Through the true company (one) meets the True One, and there is love for the True Name.
Through the True Shabad there is ever joy; at the True door (one) is found true.
O Nanak, the service of the True Guru is done by him alone on whom the Creator casts his glance of grace. ॥1॥
586.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In other service, service to another (than the Lord), life is cursed, and cursed the dwelling.
Leaving the Amrit, they cling to poison; poison is their earning, poison their capital.
Poison is their food, poison their wear, mouthfuls of poison in their mouths.
Here they earn pain upon pain, and when they die, their dwelling is in hell.
The manmukhs, with soiled faces, do not know the Shabad; they are ruined in lust and anger.
They have cast off the fear of the True Guru; through the mind's stubbornness no work comes right.
Bound in the city of Jam they are beaten; none hears their plea.
O Nanak, one does what was written beforehand; the Gurmukhs dwell in the Name. ॥2॥
586.6: Serve that True Guru, the Saadh, who has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, firm (within).
Worship day and night that True Guru who has had (us) repeat (the Name of) the Lord of the world, the Master of the universe.
Behold, every instant, that True Guru who has shown the way to the Lord, Har.
Fall, all of you, at that True Guru's feet, who has ended the darkness of attachment.
Call that True Guru blessed, blessed, all of you, who has brought (us) to the treasures of the Lord's devotion. ॥3॥
586.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Meeting the True Guru, hunger has gone; through (religious) garbs hunger does not go.
Gripped by its pain, (the garb-wearer) goes about from door to door, and in the hereafter gets twice the punishment.
Sahaj has not come within (him), so that he might take what comes and eat it in Sahaj.
Whoever he begs from with a stubborn mind, he takes (from him) only by causing distress.
Better than this garb is the householder, from whom someone gains (something).
Those dyed in the Shabad have gained understanding; (others) go astray in the doubt of duality.
One must act by the record (of past deeds) that has been laid down; nothing can be said (of it).
O Nanak, those who please him are good, whose honour you, (O Lord,) accept. ॥1॥
587.1: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
By serving the True Guru there is peace for ever, and the pain of birth and death goes.
No anxiety arises at all, (for) the Carefree (Lord) comes to dwell in the mind.
Within (oneself) is the tirath of divine knowledge; the True Guru has made this known.
The filth has gone and the mind has become pure, bathing at the tirath, the pool of Amrit.
Friends have met friends, through the True Shabad, in love.
In their own home they have found intimacy (with the Lord), merging (their) light in the Light.
With hypocrisy, Jamkaal does not let (one) go; he will carry (the hypocrite) off, his honour lost.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam are saved, fixing (their) attention on the True One. ॥2॥
587.2: Go and sit in that Sat Sangat where the Name of the Lord, Har, is churned.
(There) take the Lord's Name in Sahaj, so that the essence, the Lord, is not lost.
Repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, always, day and night, (and) shelter is found in the Lord's court.
He alone finds the perfect True Guru on whose brow, on whose forehead, it is written from the very first.
Let all bow before that Guru who has spoken the talk of the Lord, Har. ॥4॥
587.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Friends have met friends, those who love the True Guru.
Meeting together, they have meditated on the Beloved; their love rests in true affection.
From within itself the mind has come to believe, through the Guru's infinite Shabad.
These friends, once met, do not part, whom the Creator himself has united.
Some have not come to have faith in the sight (of the Guru); they do not reflect through the Shabad.
What (more) separation can the separated suffer, whose affection is caught in the love of another?
Friendship with a manmukh lasts but four short days.
This love takes no time to break; from this friendship (only) vices flow.
Those within whom there is no fear of the True One, who do not love the Naam:
O Nanak, why make friends with them, whom the Creator himself has led astray? ॥1॥
587.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Some stay ever in the love of the One; to them I am for ever a sacrifice.
I would offer them body, mind and wealth, and bow down again and again at their feet.
Meeting them, the mind is contented, and all craving and hunger go.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam are ever at peace, fixing (their) attention on the True One. ॥2॥
587.5: I am a sacrifice to that Guru who has told (me) the story of the Lord, Har.
To that Guru I am for ever a sacrifice, who has laid down the way of the Lord's service.
That beloved True Guru is with me; he sets me free wherever (I am).
Praise be to that Guru, who has given (me) understanding of the Lord.
Nanak is a sacrifice to the Guru, who has given the Lord's Name and fulfilled my mind's hope. ॥5॥
588.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Scorched by craving, (the world) has burned to death; burning and burning, it cries out.
If it meets the cooling True Guru, it will not burn again a second time.
O Nanak, without the Name no one is free of fear, so long as one does not reflect through the Shabad. ॥1॥
588.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through (religious) garbs the fire (of craving) is not quenched; anxiety remains in the mind.
Beat the snake's hole and the snake does not die: just so are the deeds of those without a Guru.
If the True Guru, the Giver, is served, the Shabad comes to dwell in the mind.
Mind and body become cool and at peace, and the fire of craving is put out.
There is lasting peace, the crown of all comforts, when one rids oneself of self-conceit from within.
Through the Guru, he alone practises (true) detachment who keeps (his) attention fixed on the True One.
No anxiety arises (in him) at all; he is fully sated with the Lord's Name.
O Nanak, without the Name there is no release; (people) burn and are consumed in Haumai. ॥2॥
588.3: Those who have meditated on the Name of the Lord, Har Har, have obtained every comfort.
Fruitful is the whole life of those in whose minds hunger for the Lord's Name has arisen.
Those who have worshipped (the Lord) through the Guru's word have forgotten all (their) sorrows.
Those Sants, the Gursikhs, are good, who do not look in the least to another (besides the Lord).
Blessed, blessed is their Guru, whose mouth bears the Lord's Amrit fruit. ॥6॥
588.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Kalyug Jam is merciless, (yet) he does (his) work only by (God's) Hukam.
Those whom the Guru has protected are saved; on the manmukhs he inflicts punishment.
The world is held bound in the power of Jamkaal, and it has no one to protect it.
Serve the One who made Jam; through the Guru, (then) no pain comes.
O Nanak, Jam serves the Gurmukhs, in whose minds the True One is. ॥1॥
588.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
This body is full of disease; without the Shabad the pain, the disease of Haumai, does not go.
If the True Guru is met, then one becomes pure and enshrines the Lord's Name alone in the mind.
O Nanak, (those who) have meditated on the Name of the Giver of peace have forgotten (their) pain, in Sahaj and in love. ॥2॥
588.6: The Guru who has taught (me of) the Life of the world: to that Guru I am ever a sacrifice.
To that Guru I am cut in pieces as a sacrifice, who has made (me) hear the Name of the Lord, Madhusudan.
To that Guru I am offered up, who has rid (me) of the poison of Haumai, the whole disease.
Great is the good done by that True Guru who, cutting away (my) failings, has made (me) understand the Lord of virtues.
That True Guru has met those on whose face and brow (good) fortune was written and set. ॥7॥
589.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The marjeevre, dead (to self) while alive, perform devotion; through the Guru, devotion goes on for ever.
On them (the Lord) has bestowed from the very first the treasure of devotion; no one can erase it.
Within the mind they have found the Treasure of virtues, the one True Lord.
O Nanak, through the Guru they remain united (with him), and never again is there separation. ॥1॥
589.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(The one who) has not served the True Guru: what reflection can he make?
He does not know the worth of the Shabad; the fool is lost in the poison (of Maya).
The blind, ignorant one performs many (ritual) deeds, (but his) affection is caught in the love of another.
Being nothing, they count themselves (great); Jam strikes them and brings them to ruin.
O Nanak, to whom is one to speak, when (the Lord) himself is the Forgiver? ॥2॥
589.3: You are the Creator, you know everything; all beings are yours.
Whomever you will, you join to yourself; what (power) have the poor creatures?
You are the all-powerful Cause of creation, O True Creator.
The one whom you unite (with yourself), O Beloved, meets you, reflecting (on you) through the Guru.
I am a sacrifice to my own True Guru, by whom my Lord, the Unknowable, has been made known (to me). ॥8॥
589.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who is an assayer of jewels reflects on jewels.
The ignorant one, blind and in darkness, does not know the worth of jewels.
The jewel is the Guru's Shabad; one who has understanding understands (this).
Fools count themselves (great); they die and are born (again), and are ruined.
O Nanak, the jewels are found by the one in whom love wells up through the Guru.
He utters the Naam for ever and ever; the Lord's Name alone is his daily dealing.
If (the Lord) shows his own grace, then I may keep the Lord enshrined in my heart. ॥1॥
589.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have not served the True Guru, nor come to love the Lord's Name:
do not think they are alive; the Creator himself has struck them dead.
Haumai is a great disease; (in it) one acts in the love of another.
O Nanak, the manmukhs are dead while alive; forgetting the Lord, they suffer pain. ॥2॥
589.6: One whose inner heart is pure: before that person all bow.
One within whom is the treasure of the Naam: to that person I am a sacrifice.
One within whom is a discerning intellect, (and) the Name of the Lord, Murari:
that True Guru is the friend of all; all are dear to him.
The Lord who pervades every soul has spread out all (this): so the Guru's understanding has seen. ॥9॥
589.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without serving the True Guru, the deeds (people) do in Haumai are bonds for the soul.
Without serving the True Guru, they find no resting place; they die and are born, and come and go.
Without serving the True Guru, (their) speech is insipid, and the Naam does not dwell in the mind.
O Nanak, without serving the True Guru, (such people) are tied up and beaten in Jam's city, and go from here with blackened faces. ॥1॥
590.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Let me burn such a way (of life) through which I forget the Beloved.
O Nanak, that love alone is good through which one's honour is kept with the Master. ॥2॥
590.2: Serve the Lord, the one Giver; meditate on the one Lord.
Ask of the Lord, the one Giver, (and) what the mind longs for is obtained.
If one asks of another, one dies of shame.
Whoever has served (him) has obtained the fruit; all the hunger of that servant is taken away.
Nanak is a sacrifice to those who meditate night and day on the Lord's Name in their hearts. ॥10॥
590.3: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
My Beloved is himself pleased with (his) devotees; he himself has attached (his) servants (to himself).
To the devotees he has given kingship; the Lord has fashioned the true royal canopy over their heads.
Doing the True Guru's work, they are ever at peace and pure.
Those are not to be called kings who fight and die, and then fall into (the round of) births.
O Nanak, without the Name they go about with their noses cut off (in disgrace), and win no honour at all. ॥1॥
590.4: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Hearing the teaching (alone), no relish has come, so long as one is not joined, through the Guru, to the Shabad.
By serving the True Guru the Naam dwells in the mind, and doubt and fear flee from within.
When one becomes such as one knows the True Guru to be, then (one's) attention is fixed on the True Name.
O Nanak, through the Name greatness is received, and (such ones) shine at the Lord's door hereafter. ॥2॥
590.5: In the minds of the Gursikhs is love for the Lord; they come to worship the Guru.
With love they trade in the Lord's Name, and carry away the Lord's Name as (their) profit.
The faces of the Gursikhs are radiant; they are pleasing in the Lord's court.
The Guru, the True Guru, is the heap (of threshed grain) of the Lord's Name; the fortunate Sikhs enter into partnership (with him) in virtues.
I am a sacrifice to those Gursikhs who keep meditating on the Lord's Name as they sit and as they rise. ॥11॥
590.6: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O Nanak, the Naam is the treasure; it is found through the Guru.
The manmukhs do not know the thing that lies in their own house; the blind ones die barking and wailing. ॥1॥
590.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Golden and spotless is the body that, through the True Name, is joined to the True One.
It has found the Immaculate One, the spotless Light; through the Guru, its doubt and fear have fled.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs, night and day detached (from the world) in longing for the Lord, ever find peace. ॥2॥
590.8: Blessed, blessed are those Gursikhs who have heard with their own ears the Guru's teaching of the Lord.
The one in whom the Guru, the True Guru, has made the Naam firm has shattered Haumai and duality.
Apart from the Lord's Name there is no friend: the Lord's servants have reflected and seen it so.
The Gursikhs with whom the Lord is pleased have accepted the True Guru's word.
Those who meditate on the Naam through the Guru are dyed in a fourfold colour (of love). ॥12॥
591.1: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The manmukh is a coward and ill-favoured; without the Name he has no nose (no honour).
Day and night he is caught up in worldly affairs; not even in a dream does he have peace.
O Nanak, if (manmukhs) become Gurmukh, they are saved; otherwise they suffer pain, held in bonds. ॥1॥
591.2: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The Gurmukhs look ever beautiful at (the Lord's) door; they live by the Guru's Shabad.
Within them is calm and ever peace; at the true door they receive honour.
O Nanak, the Gurmukhs have obtained the Lord's Name; in Sahaj they stay merged in the True One. ॥2॥
591.3: Through the Guru, Prahlad meditated on the Lord and attained liberation.
Through the Guru, Janak fixed his attention on the Lord's Name.
Through the Guru, Basisht imparted the Lord's teaching.
No one has found the Lord's Name without the Guru, O my brother.
Through the Guru, the Lord himself has granted devotion to himself. ॥13॥
591.4: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who has not come to trust the True Guru, and whose love has not taken to the Shabad,
finds no peace welling up within, though he come and go (to the Guru) a hundred times.
O Nanak, through the Guru (the Lord) is met in Sahaj, if one fixes one's attention on the True One. ॥1॥
591.5: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O mind, search out and find such a True Guru, serving whom the pain of birth and death goes away,
no anxiety arises at all, and Haumai is burnt away through the Shabad,
the wall of falsehood is taken out from within, and the True One comes to dwell in the mind,
and there is calm within and peace in the mind, as one does one's work in the discipline of truth.
O Nanak, the True Guru is met through perfect grace, when the dear Lord shows mercy by his own will. ॥2॥
591.6: The one in whose house the Lord is the Diwan (the ruler): the whole world has come into his fist.
He is beholden to no one; the Lord, the Diwan, has brought all and set them at his feet.
From a court of men someone may run and get away, (but) from the Lord's court where could anyone go?
Such a Diwan, the Lord, dwells in the hearts of the devotees; he has brought all the rest, every last one, and made them stand before the devotees.
The glory of the Lord's Name is obtained by (his) grace; some rare one, through the Guru, has meditated (on it). ॥14॥
591.7: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Without serving the True Guru the world has died, wasting its life in vain.
In the love of another, great pain has struck it; it dies and is born, and comes and goes.
Its dwelling is in filth, and it falls into births again and again.
O Nanak, without the Name Jam will strike it down, and at the end it departs repenting. ॥1॥
591.8: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In this world there is one Purakh, the Husband; all the rest, the whole creation, is (his) bride.
He enjoys every body, yet stays untouched; he is the Unseen, and cannot be seen.
The perfect Guru has shown (him), and through the Shabad has given understanding (of him).
Those who serve the Purakh become purakhs (like him): those who have burnt Haumai through the Shabad.
He has no rival, nor any enemy to pierce him like a thorn.
His rule is unshakable for ever; he neither comes nor goes.
Night and day (his) servant serves (him) and sings the virtues of the True Lord.
Nanak has blossomed, beholding the glory of the True Lord. ॥2॥
592.1: Those in whose hearts the Lord's Name ever dwells: the Lord's Name alone is their protector.
The Lord's Name is (our) father, the Lord's Name alone (our) mother; the Lord's Name is our helper and friend.
With the Lord's Name is (our) talk, with the Lord's Name (our) counsel; the Lord's Name takes care of us every day.
The Lord's Name is our company, most dear; the Lord's Name is (our) lineage, the Lord's Name (our) family.
To servant Nanak the Guru has given the Lord's Name; the Lord ever brings (him) across, in this world and the next. ॥15॥
592.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have met the True Guru ever practise the Lord's praise.
The Name of the carefree Lord has come to dwell in their minds, and they stay merged in the True Shabad.
They save their whole lineage, and themselves attain the state of liberation.
The Supreme Lord is well pleased with the people who fall at the feet of the Guru.
Servant Nanak is a slave of the Lord; in his mercy the Lord keeps (his) honour. ॥1॥
592.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In Haumai there is dread within, and (life) passes in dread upon dread.
Haumai is a great disease; (in it one) dies and is born, comes and goes.
Those for whom it was so written from the first have met the True Guru, and God has come (to meet them).
O Nanak, by the Guru's grace they are saved, burning away Haumai through the Shabad. ॥2॥
592.4: The Lord's Name is our God: unmanifest, beyond the senses, imperishable, the all-pervading Being, the Maker.
We serve the Lord's Name, we worship the Lord's Name; (our) mind is dyed in the Lord's Name alone.
None other as great as the Lord's Name comes to mind; the Lord's Name alone sets free at the end.
The Guru, the benefactor of others, has given the Lord's Name; blessed, blessed are the father and mother of the Guru.
I ever bow to my True Guru, meeting whom I have come to know the Lord's Name. ॥16॥
592.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who has not served through the Guru, whose love has not taken to the Lord's Name,
(and) who has not tasted the savour of the Shabad, dies and is born again and again.
The blind manmukh does not remember (the Lord): for what has he come into the world?
O Nanak, those on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace cross over through the Guru. ॥1॥
592.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The True Guru alone is awake; the rest of the world sleeps in attachment and thirst.
Those who serve the True Guru stay awake: those dyed in the True Name of the treasure of virtues.
The blind manmukhs do not remember (the Lord); being born and dying, they are ruined.
O Nanak, they alone have meditated on the Naam through the Guru for whom it was so written at the Source, from the first. ॥2॥
593.1: The Lord's Name is our food of thirty-six kinds, eating which we are fully satisfied.
The Lord's Name is our clothing, wearing which we shall never again be naked, and our wish to wear anything else is gone.
The Lord's Name is our trade, the Lord's Name our business; the True Guru has made us stewards of the Lord's Name.
We have written up the account of the Lord's Name alone, and all our old subjection to Jam is gone.
Some rare one, through the Guru, has meditated on the Lord's Name: those for whom, by (his) grace, the writ of receiving it was set down at the Source. ॥17॥
593.2: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The world is ignorant and blind; it does its deeds in the love of another.
Whatever deeds it does in the love of another, pain comes rushing to strike its body.
By the Guru's grace peace wells up, when one lives by the Guru's Shabad,
does one's deeds through the True Bani, and meditates on the Naam night and day.
O Nanak, to whatever (the Lord) himself attaches (beings), to that they are attached; nothing can be said (of it). ॥1॥
593.3: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In our house is the treasure of the Naam for ever, (and) the storehouses brim with devotion.
The True Guru is the giver of life to the soul; the Giver lives for ever.
Night and day, through the Guru's Shabad, we ever sing the Kirtan of the Infinite (Lord).
We ever utter the Guru's Shabad, which deals out (the gift of the Name) age after age.
This mind (of ours) dwells ever in peace, and carries on (its) trade (in the Name) in Sahaj.
Within is the Guru's wisdom, the jewel of the Lord, which brings liberation.
O Nanak, the one on whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace obtains (it), and is found true at (his) door. ॥2॥
593.4: Blessed, blessed must that Gursikh be called who has gone and fallen at the True Guru's feet.
Blessed, blessed must that Gursikh be called who has uttered with his mouth the Lord's Name, Ram.
Blessed, blessed must that Gursikh be called whose mind has filled with bliss on hearing the Lord's Name.
Blessed, blessed must that Gursikh be called who, by serving the True Guru, has received the Lord's Name.
I ever bow to that Gursikh, the Gursikh who walks in the Guru's will. ॥18॥
593.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
By the stubbornness of the mind no one has found (him); all have grown weary of performing rites.
By the mind's stubbornness (people) put on (holy) garbs and wander, and in the love of another they have met with pain.
Riddhis and siddhis (wealth and miraculous powers) are all attachment; (through them) the Naam does not come to dwell in the mind.
Through service to the Guru the mind becomes pure, and the darkness of ignorance goes.
(When) the jewel of the Naam is revealed in the house (within), O Nanak, (one) merges in Sahaj. ॥1॥
593.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
One who has not tasted the savour of the Shabad, whose love has not taken to the Name,
speaks insipid words with his tongue, and is ruined day after day.
O Nanak, one must act by the record (of past deeds) that has been laid down; no one can erase it. ॥2॥
594.1: Blessed, blessed is our True Guru, the True Being, meeting whom calm has come to us.
Blessed, blessed is our True Guru, the True Being, meeting whom we have obtained devotion to the Lord.
Blessed, blessed is our True Guru, the Lord's devotee, by serving whom we have fixed our attention on the Lord's Name.
Blessed, blessed is our True Guru, who knows the Lord, who has shown us how to see all, enemy and friend, with an equal eye.
Blessed, blessed is the True Guru, our friend, who has formed our love for the Lord's Name. ॥19॥
594.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Husband is right at home, (yet) the bride (thinks him) gone abroad; every day she pines and remembers (him).
There is no delay in meeting (him), if she makes her intention right. ॥1॥
594.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, false is the talk one makes without love;
one holds (the Lord) good only so long as he gives and one receives. ॥2॥
594.4: The Lord who created the beings has himself protected (them).
(They) have tasted the Amrit, the True Name, as their food.
They are satisfied and fully sated, (and their) hunger is stilled.
The One pervades within all, (but) some rare one has perceived (him).
O servant Nanak, (they) have been made joyful, with God on their side. ॥20॥
594.5: Salok, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Everyone looks upon the True Guru, the whole world, all there is of it;
(but) seeing (him) brings no liberation, so long as one does not reflect on the Shabad.
(Till then) the filth of Haumai does not go, and love for the Name does not take hold.
Some (the Lord) himself has forgiven and united (with himself); they have cast off duality and the vices.
O Nanak, some, beholding the sight (of the Guru), have died (to the self) and been united, in love and affection for the True Guru. ॥1॥
594.6: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The fool, blind and ignorant, has not served the True Guru;
in the love of another, great pain has struck him, and he cries out as he burns.
Those for whose sake he forgot the Guru are of no help (to him) at the final hour.
O Nanak, through the Guru's teaching (one) has found peace; the Forgiver forgives (that one). ॥2॥
594.7: (O God,) you are all by yourself, and you yourself are the Maker of everything; were there any second, only then could we call him another.
The Lord himself speaks and himself makes (all) speak; the Lord himself pervades the water and the land.
The Lord himself kills and the Lord himself spares; O mind, let us stay fallen at the Lord's refuge.
Without the Lord no one can kill or give life; (so), O mind, let us rest free of care, at ease, with limbs stretched out.
Rising, sitting and sleeping, ever and always, let us meditate on the Lord's Name; O servant Nanak, through the Guru the Lord is found.
